Let $S_m$ be the Schur multiplier with symbol $m$. We characterize the boundedness of $S_m:\mathcal S^1\to\mathcal S^{1,\infty}$ by approximation of weighted columns in a common finite-dimensional subspace. If $W(m)$ is the weak $(1,1)$ bound and $\fD(m)$ is the column approximation constant, then $\tfrac12W(m)\le\fD(m)\le2W(m)$. These estimates hold uniformly under amplification. Our second main result is the one-dimensional Hörmander--Mikhlin--Schur weak $(1,1)$ estimate. This settles the one-dimensional case of the weak $(1,1)$ problem stated in Parcet's ICM 2026 survey. The proof uses two adjacent dyadic grids and block decompositions indexed by finite binary trees. We apply Cuculescu's projections to the associated block-diagonal filtration. The resulting tree estimate is independent of the depth and grows as $2^{r/2}$ with the descendant complexity $r$.
☆ Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis
Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
☆ LLCT: Learnable Linear Canonical Transform Family with Stability for Visual Feature Processing
Zunwei Fu, Zhen Wang, Dachun Yang, Shuhui Yang
Visual structures are often characterized by directional geometry, local oscillation, and spatial--frequency coupling. To overcome the limitations of conventional spatial convolutions mainly operating on fixed Euclidean coordinates, this article develops the learnable linear canonical transform (LLCT) framework that learns parameters within the linear canonical transform (LCT) family. The framework treats the LCT family as parameterized analytical views spanning spatial, Fourier, and intermediate linear canonical representations. The framework has the following two complementary modes. The Linear Canonical Riesz Transform (LCRT) mode combines learned linear canonical coordinates with regularized Riesz-type directional responses at sites chosen for geometric and local-structural refinement. The learnable LCT mode provides the integrated responses for latent feature sites. We establish the parameter stability of the LCT representation under admissible perturbations of the canonical matrices. Both modes use chirp multiplication and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) to preserve feature dimensions and support automatic differentiation. Experiments on crack segmentation and single-image deraining evaluate the above two modes with multiple backbones. On four segmentation backbones, the full LCRT mode gives the highest reported point estimates of F1 and IoU for the crack class among the tested variants. The learnable LCT mode gives higher values in 30 of 32 paired PSNR and SSIM measurements across four deraining backbones and four datasets. In ablation studies, the full model has the highest reported PSNR and SSIM among five tested configurations.

☆ Expansive operators on Fréchet spaces without continuous norm

We investigate the existence of (metrically) expansive operators on Fréchet spaces without continuous norm. We first solve a problem posed by Bernardes, Caraballo, Darji, Fávaro, and Peris in 2025, by showing that there is no expansive operator on the Fréchet space $ω$ of all sequences. We then give examples of expansive operators on some other Fréchet spaces without continuous norm.

☆ Continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces
Pierre-A. Vuillermot
In this article we prove the existence of continuous and compact embeddings for a class of modular sequence spaces generated by Orlicz functions. The class under consideration contains sequence spaces of Orlicz-Sobolev type, including certain special cases that have played an important role in a number of applications regarding problems arising in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, as well as Nakano's class of Lebesgue sequence spaces with variable exponents. In a few exceptional cases we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for such embeddings to hold, in many others only sufficient conditions and in that situation we clearly indicate why these are not necessary by means of additional criteria and specific examples. Our results are complementary to those already available in the literature. We illustrate them with several concrete examples.

In particular, a surjective sphere isometry induces a natural correspondence between the geometric tripotents of the underlying spaces and preserves the principal structural features determined by the Peirce decomposition. These results provide a geometric framework for studying linear extension problems for sphere isometries. As an application, we establish a positive solution of Tingley's problem for finite-dimensional real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces satisfying the joint Peirce property. We also obtain an extension result for a wider class of real neutral strongly facially symmetric spaces admitting an appropriate approximation by finite-dimensional Peirce subspaces. In these settings, every surjective isometry between unit spheres extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the ambient spaces. The results demonstrate that the facial and tripotent structures play a decisive role in the rigidity of spherical isometries.

Xingyu Zhang, Dong Qiu
Xi and Zhao established a first variation formula for affine inequalities involving radial mean bodies, and asked two geometric questions about the resulting stationarity equation: whether the bodies already known to satisfy it are the only ones, and whether its smooth solutions are exactly the ellipsoids. We answer both. Every strictly convex solution of the equation with $q>-1$, $q\ne0,n$ is an ellipsoid, which answers the second question affirmatively while replacing smoothness and everywhere positive Gauss curvature by strict convexity. Every full-dimensional facet-transitive polytope satisfies the equation, and so does the polar of every vertex-transitive polytope with respect to its volume centroid; the rhombic dodecahedron, the thirteen Catalan solids and the bipyramids over regular polygons other than the octahedron provide infinitely many affinely inequivalent solutions that are not affine images of regular polytopes or balls, so the answer to the first question is negative. The rigidity proof compares overlap integrals along a continuous Steiner path: stationarity forces an increase of order $o(t)$, whereas a nonaffine chord midpoint function forces an increase of order $t$. For negative parameters the required comparison rests on a minimization formula over bounded measurable auxiliary sets.

Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira
The construction of a coherent and general integration procedure is the central question of this second part of our study of measure theory in convergence spaces. We define, and establish convergence theorems for such process of integration, called the net Riemann integration, in convergence groups and commutative monoids, preserving the prescribed convergence throughout. The underlying interchange theorem admits noncommutative groups and requires right completeness only at the cardinality of the error family. Under intrinsic stability assumptions, countable error control therefore needs only sequential completeness, even for arbitrary integration nets, from which we also stablish a general version of Henstock's lemma. The resulting uniform theorems reaches incomplete ranges in which no complete subspace contains a tail of the approximating integrals. In the ordered locally solid convergence theory side, countability of the inner direction replaces countable accessibility of the approximants, and local existence arguments yield monotone and dominated convergence and, under additional controller assumptions, a further extension through increasing integrable barriers with pointwise coverage and uniformly vanishing excess primitives. This constructs the limiting integral without a common integrable envelope and gives uniform control of primitive variation. We finish with two appendices on new and general results of abstract metrization of net convergences and related topics.

♻ ☆ Extreme points of the unit balls and isometries of noncommutative quasi-Banach Marcinkiewicz spaces

We characterize extreme points of the (positive) unit balls of Marcinkiewicz spaces with respect to their natural quasi-norms. Having these results at hand, we show that every positive surjective isometry on a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space is of elementary form. In particular, a linear mapping on a noncommutative Marcinkiewicz space over an atomic von Neumann algebra with all atoms having the same trace is a positive surjective isometry if and only if it is the restriction of a Jordan $*$-isomorphism which preserves the singular value functions. We also study (not necessarily positive) surjective isometries on weak $L_p$-spaces affiliated a $σ$-finite non-atomic von Neumann algebra for $10$, as well as one-parameter groups of isometries on the latter two.
♻ ☆ Sharp Asymptotics for $k$-Positivity Shifts under Singular Perturbations
Mohsen Kian
We show that, as the Choi matrix of a completely positive perturbation direction approaches a singular limit, the shift required for $k$-positivity can diverge more slowly than that required for complete positivity. For every $k\geq 2$, we construct a $(k-1)$-positive map $Φ$ and a completely positive map $Γ$ on $\mathbb{M}_{k+1}$ with singular Choi matrix $\mathbf{C}_Γ$. Regularizing $Γ$ by $Γ_\varepsilon=Γ+\varepsilonΔ$, where $Δ(X)=\mathrm{Tr}(X)I$, we determine the least $t\geq 0$ for which $Φ+tΓ_\varepsilon$ is $j$-positive. More precisely, $s_{j,Γ_\varepsilon}(Φ)=0$ for $j0$ is determined explicitly. The fractional exponent is obtained through singular-value estimates and an explicit construction of rank-$k$ perturbations of a nilpotent Jordan block.
♻ ☆ Non-Archimedean Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger and Non-Archimedean Maccone-Pati Uncertainty Principles
K. Mahesh Krishna
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a non-Archimedean Hilbert space over a conjugated non-Archimedean valued field $\mathbb{K}$ with $\operatorname{Char}(\mathbb{K})\neq 2$. Let $A: \mathcal{D}(A)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ and $B: \mathcal{D}(B)\subseteq \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{X}$ be possibly unbounded self-adjoint linear operators. For $x \in \mathcal{D}(A)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, define $ Δ_x(A):= \|Ax- \langle Ax, x \rangle x \|.$ Then for all $x \in \mathcal{D}(AB)\cap \mathcal{D}(BA)$ with $\langle x, x \rangle =1$, we show that \begin{align*} (1) \quad Δ_x(A)+Δ_x(B)\geq \max\{Δ_x(A), Δ_x(B)\}\geq \frac{\sqrt{\bigg|\big\langle [A,B]x, x \big\rangle ^2+\big(\langle \{A,B\}x, x \rangle -2\langle Ax, x \rangle\langle Bx, x \rangle\big)^2\bigg|}}{\sqrt{|2|}} \end{align*} and \begin{align*} (2) \quad Δ_x(A)+Δ_x(B)\geq \max\{Δ_x(A), Δ_x(B)\} \geq |\langle (A+B)x, y \rangle |, \quad \forall y \in \mathcal{X} \text{ satisfying } \|y\|\leq 1, \langle x, y \rangle =0. \end{align*} Inequality (1) may be regarded as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Heisenberg-Robertson-Schrodinger uncertainty principle, while Inequality (2) serves as a non-Archimedean analogue of the Maccone-Pati uncertainty principle.

♻ ☆ Deep kernel hedging
Jean-Loup Dupret, Donatien Hainaut, Edouard Motte
We introduce a deep kernel hedging framework that combines the flexibility of deep learning with the structural inductive bias of kernel methods. The hedging functional is restricted to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose kernel is parameterized through a neural network embedding of the input features. The framework minimizes a regularized empirical risk under convex loss functions and can accommodate path-dependent information through truncated time-augmented signature features. We derive a generalized representer theorem for the joint hedging problem, reducing the empirical optimization to a finite-dimensional problem. To further reduce the computational cost associated with large kernel matrices, we develop a scalable random Fourier feature approximation and establish convergence guarantees. The random Fourier parameters are sampled once and remain fixed throughout training, while the deep kernel adapts to market data through the learned neural representation. We evaluate the performance of the proposed deep kernel approach on both synthetic and real data and compare it with standard kernel methods and classical deep hedging architectures. Numerical results indicate competitive and robust hedging performance, particularly in low-data regimes, which highlights the benefits of combining expressive neural representations with the inductive bias of kernel methods.
♻ ☆ Projection geometry and relaxed quasi-orthogonality for inf-sup stable Galerkin methods
Tsogtgerel Gantumur
We give an elementary, coordinate-free proof that uniformly inf-sup stable nested Petrov-Galerkin methods on Hilbert spaces satisfy relaxed general quasi-orthogonality. More precisely, for any window of $N$ consecutive levels, the sum of squared Galerkin increments is bounded by the squared error at the beginning of the window times $N^σ$, where $σ<1$. The exponent $σ$ and the prefactor can be chosen explicitly in terms of the uniform projection bound. The proof uses Hilbert-space projection estimates, dyadic iteration, and duality, without relying on matrix factorizations. As a corollary, we obtain explicit growth bounds for finite block-LU factors. In the symmetric indefinite case, the positive and negative spectral splittings of the Galerkin detail spaces yield a characterization of full quasi-orthogonality in terms of uniform boundedness of the associated finite-window sign operators. We also construct a self-adjoint involution and a nested, uniformly inf-sup stable Galerkin sequence for which full general quasi-orthogonality fails. For every $0<α<1$, the construction yields a hierarchy whose finite-window constants have growth of exact order $N^α$, along with an explicit target whose Galerkin increments are not square summable.

♻ ☆ The strong reproducing kernel thesis for Hankel operators and the Garsia norm
Konstantin M. Dyakonov
Given a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ and a bounded operator $T$ on $\mathcal H$, we say that $T$ obeys the strong reproducing kernel thesis (SRKT) if $\|T\|=\sup_k\|Tk\|$, where $k$ ranges over the normalized reproducing kernels in $\mathcal H$. Two problems are posed. One of these is to determine which Hankel operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ obey the SRKT. The other concerns the geometry of the unit ball of $BMO$ with respect to the Garsia norm.

Let \(X:M^n\to\mathbb R^{n+p}\) be an \(n\)-dimensional complete self-shrinker in arbitrary codimension \(p\ge 1\). Suppose that the scalar curvature \(R\) is a positive constant and that the squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form satisfies \(S\le 1\). We prove that \(S\equiv 1\) and that \(X\) is isometric to either the round sphere \(S^n(\sqrt n)\) or the standard generalized cylinder \(S^k(\sqrt k)\times\mathbb R^{n-k}\), \(2\le k\le n-1\). The proof uses an algebraic lemma which yields a uniform positive lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci curvature, together with the comparison theorem of Wei--Wylie, the equivalence of finite Gaussian volume and polynomial volume growth due to Cheng--Zhou, and the gap theorem of Cao--Li.

We prove that every separable infinite-dimensional Fréchet algebra $X$ admits a continuous linear operator $T$ supporting a dense invariant hypercyclic algebra, giving an affirmative answer to a question of Bayart, Costa Jr. and Papathanasiou. In fact, every dense countable-dimensional subalgebra $\mathcal A$ of $X$ can be prescribed as an invariant hypercyclic algebra. When $X$ admits a continuous norm, the operator can additionally be chosen in the form $T=I+K$, where $K$ is nuclear, so that $\mathcal A = \operatorname{span} \operatorname{Orb}(a,T)$ for any prescribed $a\in\mathcal A\backslash\{0\}$.

☆ Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
Igor Kozyrev
An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $γ\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $γ$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $π/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.

☆ Branching explosion of Brownian Fleming-Viot systems
Yaohui Lin, Tiankui Lu
We resolve the long-standing non-extinction problem for Brownian Fleming-Viot systems in bounded domains. For every fixed N >= 3, we construct a bounded connected domain in R3 in which branching explosion occurs with positive probability before every prescribed positive time, from every interior initial configuration. On this event all particles converge to one boundary point. Together with two-particle non-extinction, this gives the sharp population threshold for bounded-domain Brownian explosion. The mechanism is directed transport generated by uniform copying in a periodic absorbing environment. We compute a positive cubic current for the same two-harmonic killing profile at every N >= 3, with an explicit population coefficient and a controlled fourth-order remainder. To realize this transport by spherical absorption, we develop a marked genealogical transfer theorem that retains the Euclidean displacement inherited at each copy. Common ancestry makes the integer winding reconstructible from phase records and yields convergence of the stationary signed current. A boundary restart law with P'olya weights supplies the continuity needed to turn that current into stable escape. Diffusion coefficients adapted to a common Kelvin clock preserve the joint Brownian law and uniform donor marks while compressing escape into finite lifetime. Disjoint spherical holes in a ball accumulate only at the explosion point. The boundary is smooth elsewhere, with finite area and perimeter. Boundary area within distance r of the singularity is of order r. For three particles, the transfer theorem covers every smooth positive periodic killing rate.

The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.

☆ Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
Gabriele Nani, Simone Vincini
In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $Γ$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.

Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. ☆ The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution

We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. ☆ Near-boundary rigidity and strict maximum modulus for Neumann eigenfunctions on convex planar domains

We prove that the maximum modulus of every nonzero second Neumann eigenfunction on a bounded convex planar domain $Ω$ is attained only on the boundary, without boundary smoothness or eigenvalue simplicity. The bulk model accounts for inertia, a nonsimple elastic energy depending on the second deformation gradient, and a frame-indifferent dissipation. Orientation preservation is ensured by the energy, while self-interpenetration of the limiting membrane is prevented by a uniform averaged invertibility condition. Our analysis relies on a hyperbolic minimizing movements scheme with two time-scales, which recasts the evolution into a hierarchy of incremental, sequential, and time-delayed problems. For fixed thickness, we prove the existence of solutions to the scheme and their convergence to a weak solution of the continuous-time problem as the time-scales vanish. We then identify the membrane limit at each level of the hierarchy, proving the $Γ$-convergence of the incremental functionals and the convergence of solutions to the sequential and time-delayed problems. Since the constant in the Korn inequality is not uniform in the thickness, these limits rely on estimates for the time derivative of the Cauchy-Green tensor rather than for the velocity gradient. Finally, as the outer time-scale vanishes, the membrane time-delayed solutions converge to a measure-valued solution of the membrane continuous-time problem.

In some regimes, we derive the Wave Kinetic equation associated with the equation in dimension d $\ge$ 5, almost up to the kinetic time to the power d/(d + 1). Our analysis relies on the ideas introduced by Deng and Hani.
♻ ☆ Uniqueness of Leray-Hopf weak solutions to the two-dimensional viscous Primitive Equations

Global existence of Leray-Hopf (type) weak solutions to the viscous primitive equations in two or three dimensions was established by Lions--Temam--Wang \cite{Lions1,Lions2,Lions3,Lions4} in the 1990s; however, the corresponding uniqueness, no matter in two or three dimensions, has been a long standing open problem since then. In this paper, we solve this open problem in the two-dimensional case. Precisely, we prove the uniqueness of Leray-Hopf weak solutions, with arbitrary $L^2$ initial data, to the viscous primitive equations in a periodic channel, subject to impermeability and stress-free boundary conditions on the solid boundaries.
♻ ☆ Nonexistence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue near the round sphere in low dimensions
Bruno Premoselli, Jérôme Vétois
We consider the problem of minimizing the second conformal eigenvalue of the conformal Laplacian in a conformal class of metrics with renormalized volume. We prove, in dimensions $n\in\left\{3,\dotsc,10\right\}$, that a minimizer for this problem does not exist for metrics sufficiently close to the round metric on the sphere. This is in striking contrast with the situation in dimensions $n \ge 11$, where Ammann and Humbert obtained the existence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue on any smooth closed non-locally conformally flat manifold. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also obtain a lower bound on the energy of sign-changing solutions of the \nobreak Yamabe equation in dimensions 3, 4 and 5, which extends a result obtained by Weth in the case of the round sphere.

♻ ☆ On the passage from nonlinear to linearized viscoelastodynamics
Barbora Benešová, Malte Kampschulte, Martin Kružík
The equations of linearized viscoelastodynamics in Kelvin-Voigt rheology are rigorously derived from a nonlinear model that satisfies the time-dependent frame indifference in the sense of Antman. Besides showing the convergence of corresponding solutions of both systems, we also prove the convergence of time-discrete solutions on various scales and of continuous solutions of nonlinear problems to linearized ones.
♻ ☆ Suppression of blow-up in the 3D Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system via non-parallel shear flows

In this paper, we consider the three-dimensional Patlak-Keller-Segel system coupled with the Navier-Stokes equations near the non-parallel shear flow $( Ay, 0, Ay )$ in $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$. We show that if the shear flow is sufficiently strong (A is large enough), then the solutions to Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system are global in time without any smallness restriction on the initial cell mass as long as the initial velocity satisfies $A^{\frac{2}{3}}\|u_{\rm in}\|_{H^2}\leq C_0$, which seems to be the first result of studying the suppression effect of shear flows for the 3D Patlak-Keller-Segel-Navier-Stokes system. Moreover, it implies that the solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations are global in time if the initial velocity satisfies $A^{\frac{2}{3}}\|v_{\rm in}-(Ay,0,Ay)\|_{H^2}\leq C_0,$ which also shows the transition threshold for the shear flow $(Ay,0,Ay)$ in $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.

♻ ☆ Global Analysis of the Gray-Scott Model with Fractional-Classical Diffusion
Md Shah Alam
We analyze the Gray-Scott reaction--diffusion system on $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 1$) with mixed diffusion combining local and nonlocal operators. Using semigroup methods and duality estimates, we prove global existence of component-wise nonnegative solutions and establish uniform-in-time bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate pattern formation and highlight qualitative differences between the purely local and mixed-diffusion models.
♻ ☆ On the singular set of the free boundary for a Monge-Ampère obstacle problem
Tianling Jin, Xushan Tu, Jingang Xiong
This is a continuation of our earlier work [14] on the Monge-Ampère obstacle problem \[ \det D^2 v = v^q χ_{\{v>0\}}, \quad v \geq 0 \text{ convex} \] with $q \in [0,n)$, where we studied the regularity of the strictly convex part of the free boundary. In this work, we examine the non-strictly convex part of the free boundary and establish optimal dimension bounds for its flat portion. Additionally, we investigate the strong maximum principle and a stability property for this Monge-Ampère obstacle problem.

♻ ☆ Inverse Problems for the Monge-Ampère Equation: Linearization and Nonlinear Recovery
Gunther Uhlmann, Philipp Zimmermann
We study inverse boundary value problems for the fully nonlinear Monge-Ampère equation $ \det D^2u=a(x,u,\nabla u) $ in a bounded domain. Motivated by Calderón-type problems, we introduce nonlinear Cauchy data and investigate the recovery of $a$ from boundary measurements. Around a strictly convex background solution, under a sign condition ensuring invertibility of the linearized Dirichlet problem, we establish local well-posedness and differentiable dependence on boundary data. The first variation yields a linear elliptic operator with principal coefficient given by the cofactor of the background Hessian and lower-order coefficients determined by derivatives of $a$. An Alessandrini-type identity reduces equality of nonlinear measurements to an anisotropic Calderón problem. Conditional on uniqueness for this linear problem, we recover the first derivatives of $a$ along the background jet. Higher-order linearization yields integral identities whose inversion depends on a product-density property. We also establish unconditional uniqueness results in special settings. For $\det D^2u=f(x)$, local nonlinear Cauchy data determine $f$ in dimension two, and in higher dimensions under real-analytic anisotropic hypotheses. We compare this result with a planar small-data method and an all-dimensional large-data approach based on the Euclidean X-ray transform. For semilinear nonlinearities around $Φ(x)=|x|^2/2$, Schrödinger inverse results recover the accessible $z$-jet. For equilibrium optimal-transport nonlinearities, linearization yields an isotropic conductivity equation and uniquely determines the transport density.

♻ ☆ Modified scattering for semiclassical Bose-Fermi mixtures
Kieran Cavanagh
The Vlasov-Hartree system models a mixture of bosons and fermions interacting via Coulomb forces in which the bosons are described quantum-mechanically, while the fermions are described classically. For small initial data, we prove that the system exhibits modified scattering, i.e. the bosonic and fermionic subsystems each converge to solutions of the free Schrödinger and Vlasov equations respectively, but with coupled logarithmic corrections owing to the long-range nature of Coulomb interactions. We use a mixed Lagrangian and Fourier-based approach to derive explicit descriptions of the asymptotic dynamics of the solution and associated fields and Lagrangian trajectories. Notably, due to our purely Lagrangian analysis on the Vlasov side, we require no derivatives on the initial fermion density, the asymptotic fermionic profile is as regular as the initial data, and convergence occurs in almost the same space as the initial data.

♻ ☆ Higher integrability for parabolic PDEs with generalized Orlicz growth
Peter Hästö, Jihoon Ok
We prove higher integrability of the gradient of weak solutions to nonlinear parabolic systems whose prototype is \[ \partial_t u-\mathrm{div}\Big(\frac{\varphi'(z, |\nabla u|)}{|\nabla u|}\nabla u\Big) =0, \qquad u=(u^1,\dots,u^N), \] where $\varphi$ is a generalized Young function. Special cases of our main theorem include previously known results for the $p$-growth, the variable exponent and the double phase growth. Also included are previously unknown borderline double phase growth and perturbed variable exponent growth, among others. The problem is controlled by a natural requirement of comparison of $\varphi$ between points in intrinsic parabolic cylinders via an (A1)-condition, which unifies disparate conditions from the special cases. Moreover, we handle both the singular and degenerate cases at the same time, providing a unified proof of of a reverse Hölder type inequality.

♻ ☆ Microlocal defect functionals in VMO: Geometric localisation and applications to highly heterogeneous media
Marin Mišur
We extend the concept of microlocal defect functionals to test functions belonging to the space $\mathrm{L}^\infty\cap\mathrm{VMO}_c$. Following L.~Tartar's remark that an extension of such concepts to $\mathrm{VMO}$ spaces should be possible, we establish a functional-analytic framework for this extension within the $\mathrm{L}^p-\mathrm{L}^q$ setting. Because the topological dual of $\mathrm{VMO}$ is the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^1$, the resulting object takes the form of an H-distribution rather than a non-negative Radon measure. By assuming strict Hölder conjugate inequalities, we use the John-Nirenberg inequality over localized domains to construct these functionals. We show that the functional acts as a distribution on the inductive limit topology of the test spaces, giving geometric localisation principles for equations with rough $\mathrm{VMO}$ coefficients, that is, coefficients admitting sharp transitions of vanishing mean oscillation. We illustrate the framework in three settings: stratified transport, zero-order non-local cross-phase energies, and sub-critical acoustic scattering in high-contrast media. These differ in the nonlinearity generating the companion sequence but share a common geometric conclusion, since in each case the macroscopic energy defect is confined to the characteristic variety of the underlying flow, being supported where $\sum_j a_j({\bf x})ξ_j=0$.

♻ ☆ Homothetic Self-Similar Solutions to the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
Tim Binz, Matei P. Coiculescu
We investigate homothetic forward self-similar solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: the solutions $\overline{U}$ for which both $\overline{U}$ and $β\overline{U}$ are self-similar profiles for some nontrivial $β$. Homothetic solutions are, in addition, the only solutions for which a singular limit argument can be used to prove non-uniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions along the lines of the Jia-Šverák program. In three dimensions, and for sufficiently regular initial data, we prove a Liouville theorem that rules out the existence of non-trivial homothetic solutions. In two dimensions, our Liouville theorem reproves a result of Luo and Shvydkoy that the only decaying homothetic solution with continuous angular data is the Oseen vortex. In addition, we prove that the Euler equations linearized around the Oseen vortex are stable in some subspaces of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$, for example in the space of $2$-fold rotationally symmetric functions. On the other hand, we also discover a homothetic solution for which an unstable approximate eigenvalue of the linearized Euler equations exists.

☆ On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang
It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.

We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. First, we construct non-negative Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ for every $1 \leq p < \infty$. Although such bases cannot be unconditional, their basis constants can be made arbitrarily close to one. By duality, we also obtain bases with positive biorthogonal functionals and the same bounds for all $1\leq p<\infty$. Finally, we prove that $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ admits a Schauder basis consisting of translates of a single function for every $2\le p<\infty$. The generating function $f$ can be chosen to be the restriction to $\mathbb{R}$ of an entire function. For $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$.

This improves the classical characterizations of Mbekhta~\resultcite{Theorem~1.6}{MbekhtaKato}, Schmoeger~\resultcite{Theorem~4}{Schmoeger}, and Dajić and Koliha~\resultcite{Theorem~6.7}{DajicKoliha}, by removing their closedness assumptions. ♻ ☆ Stability of isometries of quantum states
Sam Looi
We prove dimension-independent Hyers--Ulam stability for surjective approximate isometries of the positive trace-class cone in both the trace and Bures metrics. Here $\varepsilon\geq0$ is a uniform upper bound on the additive error in preserving distances. Such an approximate isometry is uniformly approximated by a Wigner symmetry (a unitary or antiunitary conjugation), with error at most $9\varepsilon/2$ in the trace metric and $2\sqrt2\varepsilon$ in the Bures metric, even if it does not fix zero. For maps fixing zero, the trace bound improves to $3\varepsilon$ even under the hypothesis of $δ$-surjectivity, independently of $δ$. In infinite dimensions, we construct spectrum-preserving homeomorphisms of the full state space, including mixed states, whose distortions tend to zero in both metrics but which stay a fixed uniform distance from every Wigner symmetry. For state spaces, stability holds in each fixed finite dimension with a dimension-dependent modulus tending to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$, but no such modulus can be chosen independently of dimension.
comment: 43 pages. Comments welcome. v2: Removed the surjectivity assumption from finite-dimensional state-space stability; showed that the state-space bijections are spectrum-preserving homeomorphisms; proved uniqueness of the approximating Wigner symmetry on the cone and extended Bures stability to approximately surjective maps fixing zero
♻ ☆ An Improved Inequality between the von Neumann-Jordan and James Constants
Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu
We provide a strengthened answer to the questions posed by Alonso, Martín, and Papini [Studia Math. 188 (2008), 135--150] concerning the comparison between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants . The classical inequality $\CNJ(X)\leq J(X)$ between the von Neumann--Jordan and James constants was established by Takahashi and Kato [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 359 (2009), 602--609], Wang [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 138 (2010), 695--701], and Yang and Li [Appl. Math. Lett. 23 (2010), 277--281], while related sharp estimates were obtained by Kato and Takahashi [Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo (2) Suppl. 82 (2010), 75--91]. We sharpen this inequality to $\CNJ(X)\leq\JB(X)$, where $\JB(X)$ is the Birkhoff--James orthogonal James constant introduced by Baronti and Papini [Constr. Math. Anal. 5 (2022), 37--45]. Our proof employs optimal distance ellipses and alternating contact directions.
comment: Metadata title corrected; manuscript unchanged
♻ ☆ Fractional gradients and nonlocal PDEs in variable exponent spaces
Susana Moura, Cornelia Schneider
We develop a theory of distributional Riesz fractional gradients in variable exponent Lebesgue spaces and introduce the associated nonlocal Sobolev spaces. Moreover, Sobolev, Hardy, Morrey, and Trudinger-type inequalities are established, and a fractional fundamental theorem of calculus is derived. As an application, we study nonlinear variational problems with nonstandard growth and establish existence and Euler--Lagrange equations for minimizers.
♻ ☆ Connectedness properties of small minimal clusters in Riemannian or Finsler manifolds
Stefano Nardulli, Aldo Pratelli
We prove that in a compact Riemannian manifold, the $m$-minimal clusters of sufficiently small total volume are connected and with small diameter, while in a more general Finsler manifold they are done by at most $m$ connected components of small diameter. We apply these results to calculate the asymptotic expansion of the multi-isoperimetric profile at the first nontrivial order, for small volumes.
comment: In this second version of the paper we have improved the introduction to be more clear. The mathematics and the proofs have not been changed
♻ ☆ Connections between Essential Norm, Bhatia-Šemrl Property and Strong Subdifferentiability of Operators on Banach Spaces
C. R. Jayanarayanan, Rishit R Rajpopat
We study Birkhoff-James orthogonality in spaces of bounded linear operators between Banach spaces through the Bhatia-Šemrl property. We investigate the interplay among three key properties of bounded linear operators: strong subdifferentiability, the Bhatia-Šemrl property, and the condition that the essential norm is strictly less than the operator norm. If $X$ is a Banach space with a $1$-unconditional basis and $Y$ is any Banach space, we show that every nonzero operator $T \in B(X, Y)$ satisfying the Bhatia-Šemrl property satisfies $\|T\|_e<\|T\|$. We identify a class of pairs of Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ for which the inequality $\|T\|_e<\|T\|$ can be characterized in terms of strong subdifferentiability of the operator norm at $T$ and compactness of the norm attainment set of $T$. We also study norm one projections satisfying the Bhatia-Šemrl property and provide examples of operators that possess this property.
♻ ☆ Nonlinear Lebesgue spaces: Curves and geometry
Guillaume Sérieys
This paper is the second in a series by the author and collaborators devoted to the study of geometric and analytic properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces, that is, L^p spaces of mappings taking values in arbitrary metric spaces. The present article formalizes the pointwise description of their geometric properties---their length structure, bounds on their Alexandrov curvature as well as the definition of a velocity for absolutely continuous curves despite the lack of differential structure. To obtain this pointwise description, we first prove a nonlinear analogue of the Fubini--Lebesgue theorem, which yields an identification of L^p curves in nonlinear Lebesgue spaces with mappings taking values in the space of L^p curves. This identification of L^p curves then enables a similar identification for absolutely continuous curves, from which the pointwise description of the geometric properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces follows.
♻ ☆ Free probability via entropic optimal transport
Octavio Arizmendi, Samuel G. G. Johnston
Let $μ$ and $ν$ be compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $μ\boxplus ν$ denote their additive free convolution. We show that for all sufficiently large real $z$, \begin{equation} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \log(z - x) \, (μ\boxplus ν)(\mathrm{d}x) = \sup_Π \left\{ \mathbf{E}_Π[\log(z - (X+Y))] - H(Π\mid μ\otimes ν) \right\}, \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all couplings $Π$ of $μ$ and $ν$. Analogous formulas hold for multiplicative free convolution $μ\boxtimes ν$ and free compression $[μ]_τ$. In this way, integrals of a log-potential against free convolutions can be expressed as entropic optimal transport problems. The corresponding optimal couplings admit explicit formulas, from which the standard $R$- and $S$-transform descriptions of additive and multiplicative free convolution are recovered. In particular, the optimizer $Π_z$ encodes the subordination equations via couplings of random variables. Our approach is based on a large deviation principle on the symmetric group, combined with the quadrature method of Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava.
comment: 40 pages, updated version with improved proof of symmetric group limit and expanded applications
♻ ☆ Turán problem on the union of three intervals of equal length
Xiao-Ye Fu, Yue-Kun Li, Wei-Jie Wang, Xuan Wang
This paper addresses the Turán extremal problem on the symmetric three-interval set $Ω_λ= (-1,1) \cup (λ-1,λ+1) \cup (-λ-1,-λ+1)$, $λ\geq 0$. We establish a discrete approximation principle relating the continuous Turán problem on $Ω_λ$ to the discrete Turán problem on an associated finite discrete set. This enables the continuous problem to be exactly expressed as a limit of finite nonnegative trigonometric polynomial problems, which are equivalent to finite semidefinite programs. Using this framework, we compute the Turán constant for integer and rational parameters $λ$. We further analyze the dependence of the Turán constant on $λ$ and derive upper bounds for all $λ> 5$.
comment: 14 pages
♻ ☆ Solution to Dixmier's Problem about spectra of C*-algebras
Martino Lupini
Dixmier asked in 1967 whether the spectra of simple separable non-type-I $C^*$-algebras all have the same Borel structure. We solve the formulation using ordinary isomorphisms of quotient Borel $σ$-algebras by proving that its universal assertion is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC. Under the continuum hypothesis, all separable non-type-I spectra are measurably isomorphic, without simplicity or unitality assumptions. In the model obtained by iterating Sacks forcing for $ω_2$ stages with countable supports over a GCH ground model, a fixed simple unital universal spectrum is not measurably isomorphic to the CAR spectrum. Neither consistency direction requires a large cardinal. The Borel-definable formulation, which requires isomorphisms to admit Borel lifts between irreducible representations, has a negative answer in ZFC. For the CAR algebra $A$ and a simple separable exact crossed product $B$ associated to $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$, there is no Borel-definable injection $\widehat B\to\widehat A$. Nevertheless, all separable nuclear non-type-I spectra are Borel-definably isomorphic. We also determine the answer under several choiceless hypotheses. The axiom of determinacy together with dependent choice gives a stronger negative conclusion: the spectrum of $B$ does not even inject as a set into the spectrum of $A$. The symmetric Solovay model gives the same conclusion. Over ZF, a wellordering of the reals of order type $ω_1$ suffices for a positive answer. The finite-permutation Feferman--Levy model gives another positive answer for the full sigma-generated Borel structures. These comparisons concern the quotient structures themselves, without measure completion.
comment: 83 pages. Substantially expanded revision: distinguishes the quotient-measurable and Borel-definable formulations; adds ZFC independence via CH and the iterated Sacks model, results under choiceless hypotheses, and expanded proofs and literature comparisons
♻ ☆ Microlocal defect functionals in VMO: Geometric localisation and applications to highly heterogeneous media
Marin Mišur
We extend the concept of microlocal defect functionals to test functions belonging to the space $\mathrm{L}^\infty\cap\mathrm{VMO}_c$. Following L.~Tartar's remark that an extension of such concepts to $\mathrm{VMO}$ spaces should be possible, we establish a functional-analytic framework for this extension within the $\mathrm{L}^p-\mathrm{L}^q$ setting. Because the topological dual of $\mathrm{VMO}$ is the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^1$, the resulting object takes the form of an H-distribution rather than a non-negative Radon measure. By assuming strict Hölder conjugate inequalities, we use the John-Nirenberg inequality over localized domains to construct these functionals. We show that the functional acts as a distribution on the inductive limit topology of the test spaces, giving geometric localisation principles for equations with rough $\mathrm{VMO}$ coefficients, that is, coefficients admitting sharp transitions of vanishing mean oscillation. We illustrate the framework in three settings: stratified transport, zero-order non-local cross-phase energies, and sub-critical acoustic scattering in high-contrast media. These differ in the nonlinearity generating the companion sequence but share a common geometric conclusion, since in each case the macroscopic energy defect is confined to the characteristic variety of the underlying flow, being supported where $\sum_j a_j({\bf x})ξ_j=0$.
comment: Work in progress
♻ ☆ Regularized barycentric Rényi divergences
Milán Mosonyi
Barycentric Rényi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum Rényi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric Rényi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric Rényi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric Rényi divergence (called the minimal one) was known to admit an explicit expression. Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric Rényi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric Rényi divergence on invertible inputs. This in turn implies that if at least two of the $D^{q_x}$ are strictly larger than the Umegaki relative entropy (in a precise sense), then the resulting barycentric Rényi divergence is not even weakly additive.
comment: 27 pages. v5: Improved presentation, slightly stronger results
♻ ☆ Modular properties of affine \(\SLA{sl}{2}\) torus \(n\)-point functions
A. Zuevsky
Krauel, Shafiq and Wood (\KSW{}) realized torus \(1\)-point functions for the simple affine \voa{}s \(L(k,0)\) built from \(\alg{sl}(2)\) as vector-valued modular forms attached to a cyclic \(R\)-module structure and to the modular tensor category \(\rep{L(k,0)}\). We extend this to torus \(n\)-point functions, defined as traces of chains of \(n\) intertwining operators winding once around the \(τ\)-cycle. Every coefficient of their local (Laurent, or Puiseux) expansion about a diagonal stratum is again a \vvmf{}, lying, whenever a mild lowest weight hypothesis holds, in the very \(R\)-modules of \cite{KSW}. Giving a torus-primarity hypothesis verified below for \(\alg{sl}(2)\), the operator product expansion then reduces leading short-distance behaviour to the classified \(1\)-point theory. For \(\alg{sl}(2)\) we classify the fusion-chain conformal block spaces, identify torus \(n\)-point primary vectors, and treat \(n=2\) in detail, obtaining a \((k+1)\)-dimensional family of vector-valued Jacobi-type forms generalizing the level-\(k\) forms \(η^{3k/2}\) of \cite{KSW}. We also extend \KSW{} categorical picture, representations of \(\Bthree=\PMod(\surf{1}{1})\) built from a modular tensor category, to representations, on fusion-chain block spaces, of a mapping-class subgroup of the \(n\)-punctured torus generated by \(S\), \(T\), and adjacent braidings, with a Verlinde-type dimension formula and categorical \(S\)-, \(T\)-operators. The \(\alg{sl}(2)\) matrix form of \(S\) beyond this abstract construction remains open.

Analysis of PDEs
☆ Large Deviations of Invariant Measures of Fractional Reaction-Diffusion Equations Driven by Multiplicative Noise on R^n
Bixiang Wang, Lu Yang
In this paper, we establish large deviations of invariant measures for fractional stochastic reaction-diffusion equations with polynomial reaction term driven by unbounded multiplicative noise on R^n. Under a dissipativity condition, we first prove the Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle of solution trajectories uniformly over all initial data in L^2(R^n). The key ingredient is a positive-time L^\infty-estimate for differences of controlled solutions which is independent of all initial data and hence yields uniform convergence of controlled stochastic solutions over the entire tphase space. Then using the uniform trajectory estimates, contraction and a second-moment estimate, we further prove the large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with a good quasipotential without introducing weighted spaces or establishing exponential tightness. The non-compactness of Sobolev embeddings in R^n is circumvented by uniform spatial tail-ends estimates. This is the first result on large deviations of invariant measures of the equation with multiplicative noise on unbounded domains.
☆ What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
James M. Hyman
Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.
☆ Modeling soliton-potential interactions for the 1-D cubic NLS via an invariant-preserving finite-difference method
Anthony D. Stone, Christopher C. Hogan
We consider the 1-D focusing cubic NLS with a smooth, spatially-dependent potential which decays rapidly as $x \rightarrow \pm \infty$. As is well known, under sufficient regularity conditions, solutions of the cubic NLS with such a spatially-dependent potential conserve both mass and energy. Additionally, in the absence of a potential, the 1-D focusing cubic NLS admits boosted soliton solutions. Furthermore, in the presence of a potential, the interaction of the potential with boosted soliton solutions to the free case is of active interest in the literature, particularly with respect to the dependence of this soliton-potential interaction on the velocity of the incident soliton. We adapt a finite-difference scheme to the setting of a smooth, rapidly-decaying spatially-dependent potential and show that this adaptation preserves the appropriate mass and energy invariants. Additionally, we use this algorithm to model soliton-potential interactions at a variety of incident soliton velocities.
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures
☆ Fresnel scattering for open waveguide networks
Solomon Quinn, Charles L. Epstein
This paper concerns the Helmholtz scattering problem for open waveguide networks, extending the analysis from [arXiv:2302.04353, arXiv:2310.05816, arXiv:2401.04674] to plane-wave incident data. We first reduce the problem to a Fredholm second-kind integral equation on an infinite interface. This produces an integral representation of the solution to the original scattering problem, which is then used to obtain detailed asymptotic estimates of the solution at infinity. To leading order and away from the waveguides, the scattered field is itself a plane wave. Its amplitude and phase shift exhibit a jump across a critical polar angle depending on the direction of the incident plane-wave. Our estimates also imply that the scattered field is outgoing in a weak sense, allowing us to establish a uniqueness result. We conclude by calculating the waveguide-mode contributions to the scattered field in a perturbative regime.
☆ Kinetic SDEs and kinetic Fokker-Planck equations with critical Morrey-type drifts, and local blow-ups
Jean-François Jabir, Damir Kinzebulatov, Chengjun Yue
We develop a Sobolev theory for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation subject to a singular Morrey-form $L^\infty+M^q_K$ force field which can produce local blow-ups due to strong attraction to a submanifold. Our approach is based on the fractional representation for the Duhamel series of the equation and on establishing kinetic Adams-type estimates. Accordingly, we construct weak solutions of Brownian-driven kinetic SDEs in a critical Morrey set-up, obtain kinetic Krylov-type estimates and a strongly continuous Feller propagator, and establish uniqueness criteria for a large class of weak solutions.
☆ Higher-Order Paracontrolled Calculus for Geometric Rough Paths
Tim Van Hoose
We study the rough differential equation $$ \frac{du_t}{dt}= F(u_t) ζ_t, \ \ u(0) = u_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d, $$ where $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ is a sufficiently regular vector field, and the noise $ζ$ is a distribution in $\mathscr{C}^{α-1}(\mathbb{R})$ for $α\in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$. We construct solutions to this equation at lower regularity than previous work of Gubinelli-Imkeller-Perkowski and Prömel-Trabs using ideas from the high-order paracontrolled viewpoint of Bailleul-Bernicot. The key tool in our work is the development of a harmonic-analytic framework for proving a set of iterated commutator estimates which are necessary for the solution theory. We also show the procedure of enhancement when the noise $ζ= dZ$, where $Z$ is a realization of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H \in (\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3})$.
comment: 50 pages
☆ Norm-resolvent asymptotics for the Neumann Laplacian on periodic resonant thin structures
Kirill Cherednichenko, Chuanjie Wu
We consider the Neumann Laplacian on a three-dimensional periodic network of thin rods with edge thickness of order $h$ and vertex diameter of order $h^{2/3}$. We extend the fixed-graph resonant reduction to obtain a finite-$h$ periodic graph approximation with generalised norm-resolvent error $O(h)$, uniformly in the Floquet quasi-momentum. An exact gauge transformation identifies the phase-corrected graph fibres with the canonical lattice Floquet fibres, giving the same rate for the global operators. Collapsing the contact points while retaining the ambient edge tangents gives an approximation with error $O(h^{2/3})$. The proof uses a Ryzhov boundary triple and a Schur--Feshbach reduction. The estimates yield quantitative approximation of Bloch bands and stability of open gaps on bounded energy intervals. For the simple-cubic lattice, we refine the known resonant dispersion calculation to obtain a complete band-gap decomposition and $O(h)$ control of the persistence of each fixed finite collection of gaps in the thin structure.
☆ Resonance counting and spectral gaps for hyperbolic surfaces via Fourier decay
Louis Soares
We prove an improved fractal Weyl upper bound for resonances of infinite-area convex cocompact hyperbolic surfaces, expressed in terms of the Hausdorff dimension of the limit set and the Fourier decay exponent of the Patterson--Sullivan measure. This bound also yields a sharper upper bound for the essential spectral gap for these surfaces.
☆ Multi-peak solutions for a magnetic nonlinear Schrödinger equation with exponential critical growth in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
Pietro d'Avenia, Chao Ji, Qingyue Li
In this paper, we study the following magnetic nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{i}\nabla-A(x)\right)^{2}u+V(x)u=f(|u|^{2})u\,\ \text{in}\,\ \mathbb{R}^{2}, \] where $\varepsilon>0$ is a parameter, $A\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R}^{2})$ is a magnetic potential, $V\in C(\mathbb{R}^{2}, \mathbb{R})$ is a multi-well potential, and $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R})$ exhibits exponential critical growth. By variational methods and a penalization technique, we prove the existence and multiplicity of nontrivial solutions for sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. If, in addition, $A\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^2,\mathbb{R}^2)$, we show that these solutions have multiple peaks and we establish their concentration behavior and exponential decay.
comment: 62 pages
☆ Local well-posedness for the exponentially modified Benjamin-Ono equation
Thyago S. R. Santos
We prove local well-posedness for the modified Benjamin-Ono equation in $H^s(\mathbb{R})$ for $s>3/2$. This equation arises as a modified counterpart of the Benjamin-Ono equation through a Miura-type transformation, in close analogy with the classical relation between mKdV and KdV equations. One of the main obstacles is the apparent derivative loss in the quadratic part of the equation. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce a Cole-Hopf transform adapted to the structure of the equation. The map removes the quadratic derivative term and converts the equation into a Schrödinger equation with a transport and a commutator terms that can be controlled without derivative loss. Solutions are then constructed by parabolic regularization, while frequency envelopes are used to obtain the continuity of the data-to-solution map. In the degenerate case $γ=0$, the transform completely linearizes the equation and yields local well-posedness for every $s>1/2$, down to the scaling-critical threshold.
comment: 21 pages
☆ Analytical and numerical periodic homogenization of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations in a $W^{2,p}$ Cordes framework
Timo Sprekeler, Hung V. Tran
We study periodic homogenization of fully-nonlinear second-order Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations subject to a homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition and the numerical approximation of the effective Hamiltonian, where the diffusion matrix is assumed to satisfy the Cordes condition. In the first part, assuming the Cordes parameter is sufficiently large, we show existence and uniqueness of $W^{2,p}$ solutions to the true cell problem, prove homogenization under minimal regularity assumptions, and establish a quantitative homogenization result. In the second part, we propose and rigorously analyze $W^{2,p}$-conforming and mixed finite element methods for the approximation of the corrector, which are then used in the approximation of the effective Hamiltonian. The key tool used throughout this work is Campanato's concept of near operators.
comment: 25 pages
☆ Non-branching properties of Regular Lagrangian Flows and well posedness of the continuity equation in the class of nonnegative solutions
Luigi Ambrosio, Stefano Bianchini, Federico Renzi, Federico Vitillaro
In this paper we deal with the theory of Regular Lagrangian Flows, as initiated in [29] and axiomatized in [2]. In the first part of the paper we show in Theorem 4.3 (see also Corollary 4.5) that the decomposition of $\mathcal{L}^{1+d}$-almost all the space time in a family of (essentially) disjoint characteristics, the technique at the basis of the well posedness in [1] (for planar, divergence-free and autonomous vector fields), and in [13] (for vector fields having a suitable regularity in space, including BV vector fields) is not only sufficient for well posedness, but also necessary. This shows that in many cases the typical uniqueness statement of the DiPerna-Lions theory, namely that the path $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ is (essentially) unique given the initial position $x$, can, as in the classical theory, be strengthened by saying that the paths $\mathbb{X}(\cdot,x)$ (essentially) do not branch. As the simple Example 1.1 shows, when we consider vector fields with singular divergence well posedness results may hold only for solutions that do not change sign. In the second part of the paper we revisit [8,9] obtaining a well posedness result for special vector fields of bounded deformation and nonnegative solutions, under a mild regularity assumption (5.3) with respect to the time variable, weaker than the space-time $SBD$ regularity assumption made in [9] for nearly incompressible vector fields. Finally, we revisit carefully the constructions of Section 9 of [13], to see how they provide existence and uniqueness for (1.2) assuming $BV$ regularity in space, in the class of nonnegative bounded solutions.
☆ Sharp dimension threshold for unique FKPP steady states and BBM recurrence
Luca Rossi, Oliver Tough
We consider the existence and uniqueness of positive, bounded stationary solutions of the Fisher-KPP equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We establish that stationary solutions are unique, and exist if and only if the generalised principal eigenvalue is strictly positive (supercriticality), in dimension at most $6$. This is sharp: we exhibit examples both of non-uniqueness and of existence at criticality in dimension $7$ or higher, including for the classical reaction $f(u)=u-u^2$. This proves a conjecture of Berestycki and Graham in the affirmative for dimension at most $6$, and in the negative for dimension at least $7$. We thereby show that branching Brownian motion cannot survive globally without surviving locally in dimension $6$ or lower, but can do so in dimension $7$ or higher, mirroring the classical transition of Brownian motion from recurrence to transience from dimension $2$ to $3$. We further show that relaxing the strong-KPP condition results in a more general sharp dimension threshold for the uniqueness/non-existence result. These results are valid without any regularity assumptions on the domain boundary. As a corollary, we show that solutions of the evolution reaction-diffusion equation are always convergent in the long run in dimension at most $6$, whilst we exhibit non-convergent solutions in dimension larger than $6$.
comment: 55 pages
☆ Local Turnpike Stability for Two-Population Second-Order Mean-Field Game Systems
Mohamed Ghattassi, Fanze Kong, Nader Masmoudi
This paper establishes a local turnpike property for a two-population, second-order mean-field game system with a quadratic Hamiltonian, in which the running cost for each population may depend on both population densities. In the case of two populations, imposing a scalar stability condition separately on each species is not sufficient because it neglects cross-interaction effects. The appropriate requirement is instead a matrix-valued coercivity condition on vector perturbations $(μ_1,μ_2)$, which involves the symmetric part of the linearized interaction matrix together with weighted Poincaré inequalities associated with the two stationary measures. Consequently, in the multi-population framework, diffusion still acts independently on each population, but the interactions are controlled by the full coupling matrix. A naive scalar energy functional fails to capture mixed second-variation terms arising from costs that depend on both densities. We prove that matrix coercivity is precisely equivalent to the strict positivity of this second variation, and we provide a spectral characterization in terms of the principal spectral value of the coupled stationary linearized operator. For linear models with cross-interactions, this yields explicit algebraic conditions that separate stable parameter ranges from unstable ones. In the non-potential framework, the skew-symmetric part of the interaction matrix leaves the coercivity threshold unchanged, but it can induce transient oscillatory dynamics. Moreover, the scalar turnpike theory extends in a natural, though nontrivial, manner to multi-population systems, where stability is governed by the positivity of a coupled matrix-valued second variation that encodes both self-interactions and cross-interactions.
☆ A cell problem for the boundary density and approximation of boundary correctors in homogenization theory
Shari Moskow
We study the boundary corrector $θ_ε$ in the two-scale expansion for periodic elliptic problems with Dirichlet conditions. By results of Gérard-Varet--Masmoudi and Prange, on smooth uniformly convex domains $θ_ε$ converges to the solution $θ^*$ of a homogenized problem with boundary data given by the boundary layer tail $d(n)$, which is determined by a half-space problem for each normal $n$. In the lifted form of Gérard-Varet and Masmoudi, $d(n)$ is given explicitly by the cell correctors and the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator $N_n$ of this half-space problem. Our main result is that $N_n$ satisfies a nonlinear equation on the period cell alone, so that $d(n)$ and the boundary density that represents it can be computed on the cell. This equation is a Riccati equation in which the derivative in depth is replaced by a commutator with the derivative along $n$. This cell problem can therefore be solved by a Riccati doubling algorithm, and we can compute $d(n)$ at irrational normals without rational approximation. Dropping the commutator term in the cell equation gives an operator square root approximation for $N_n$ that captures the leading term of $d(n)$ for small contrast, for the truncated problem. Finally, we approximate $θ_ε$ at finite $ε$ by the sum of two solutions of constant coefficient problems, one with oscillatory boundary data and the other $θ^*$, and test it on the disk.
☆ Transformed Convexity for Lane--Emden Equations and Torsion on Spherical Domains
Xiuda Liang, Wenjie Wang
We study the geometry of positive Dirichlet solutions on smooth, uniformly geodesically convex domains $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb S^n$, $n\ge2$. Set $p_n^*=2n/(2n-3)$. For the Lane--Emden equation $-Δ_g u=u^p$, $10$ in $Ω$. For the torsion equation $-Δ_g u=1$, we establish $\nabla_g^2\sqrt{u}<0$ for its unique Dirichlet solution in all dimensions $n\ge2$, without an additional diameter or circumradius assumption. In both settings, the solutions specified above have a unique nondegenerate maximum and strictly geodesically convex positive superlevel sets. For the non-power reaction $f(s)=s^p/(1+λs^δ)$, with $10$, and $0<δ\le(p-1)/3$, we also prove the existence of at least one positive solution $u$ for which the transform $\left(\int_u^\infty ds/f(s)\right)^{1/3}$ has positive definite Hessian. The proofs combine a spherical Schur-complement estimate with a priori bounds and continuation.
☆ Borderline double phase functionals with powers of the logarithm: regularity in the vectorial case
Youlin Choi, Jehan Oh
We study vector-valued local minimizers of the borderline double phase functional whose integrand is $|D\mathbf{w}|^p+a(x)|D\mathbf{w}|^p\log^γ(e+|D\mathbf{w}|)$, where $p>1$, $γ>0$ and the coefficient $a(\cdot)$ is nonnegative and bounded. If the modulus of continuity $ω(\cdot)$ of $a(\cdot)$ satisfies $ω(r)\log^γ(1/r)\to0$ as $r\to0$, then minimizers are locally Hölder continuous for every exponent less than one. If $a(\cdot)$ is Hölder continuous, then the gradients of minimizers are locally Hölder continuous. In the vector-valued setting these results were previously available only for $γ=1$. The proof combines a comparison with frozen functionals, whose regularity theory applies uniformly in the frozen coefficient, with the higher integrability of minimizers.
☆ Existence and uniqueness of viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg system

We establish the existence and uniqueness, up to translation, of monotone viscous-dispersive shock profiles for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, provided the two constant end states satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot and Lax entropy conditions and the shock strength is small. Treating the small shock strength as a singular perturbation parameter, we construct the profiles via Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory. We further provide pointwise estimates for the profiles, which are used in the nonlinear stability analysis of generic Riemann solutions to the NSFK system in a companion work.

☆ Limit cycles govern wave energy accumulation in space-time-varying materials
Bryn Davies, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen
We study the amplification and concentration of wave energy in smooth, periodic space-time media through the dynamics of the characteristic curves of the associated wave equation. In an impedance-matched setting, we show that stable limit cycles attract neighbouring characteristics, focusing the wave energy density. The exponential attraction rate is estimated analytically from the system's Lyapunov exponent. We further show that the attraction of characteristics and energy accumulation persist under a range of nonperiodic perturbations. Finally, we present a Floquet-Fourier numerical method for computing stable and unstable limit cycles and their attraction rates. Throughout, we exemplify the results using the example of modulation given by a superposition of travelling waves, revealing saddle--node bifurcations where limit cycles may appear depending on the relative wave speeds. Full-wave simulations confirm that the characteristic mechanism continues to describe energy accumulation beyond the impedance-matched case.

☆ Fundamental solution expansions in stochastic homogenization of parabolic systems with time-dependent coefficients
Junxin Pan, Li Wang, Qiang Xu
This paper studies fundamental solutions of uniformly parabolic systems with stationary random coefficients depending on space and time. Under ergodicity and local regularity, we establish quenched Gaussian bounds for the kernel and its spatial derivatives, with stationary random prefactors. A spectral gap assumption gives moments of every finite order for these prefactors and hence annealed Gaussian bounds. We also prove quantitative two-scale expansions for the kernel, its spatial gradient, and its mixed spatial derivative. The error estimates hold in every finite probability moment and retain Gaussian decay. Their dimension-dependent growth is described by a corrector weight, with a single additional logarithmic factor in the derivative estimates. The proofs combine large-scale regularity, extended correctors, weighted estimates, and a parabolic weak-norm estimate. The latter supplies the passage from deterministic pairings to local annealed estimates without interchanging expectation and a supremum over test functions. The mixed-derivative estimate builds on the gradient expansion and does not introduce a further logarithmic loss.

☆ Gauge Transforms and Strichartz Estimates for Benjamin--Ono-Type Dirac Equations
Nelson Faustino
For $T>0$, we consider the Benjamin--Ono-type Dirac equation $$ i\partial_tψ(x,t) + D(-Δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}ψ(x,t) = D\,G(ψ(x,t)), \qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times[0,T], $$ where $(-Δ)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is the fractional Riesz operator, $D$ is the Dirac operator associated with the Clifford algebra of signature $(0,n)$, and $G(\cdot)$ a scalar-valued quadratic nonlinearity. Under a pointwise anti-commutation condition on $ψ$ and a uniform dyadic regularity assumption on its spatial Fourier profile, we construct a unit-modulus gauge map $u$ by $ u=\exp\bigl(-iw\bigr),$ where $w$ is a solution of $Dw=ψ$. Assuming, in addition, the stated regularity and commutation conditions on $w$, we show that the Plemelj components $u_{\pm}=P_{\pm}u$ solve a coupled Schrödinger system with gauge nonlinearities $P_{\pm}N(ψ,u)$, where $$ N(ψ(x,t),u(x,t)) = -2P_{-}\!\left[ G(ψ(x,t)) \right]u(x,t). $$ We also obtain a priori estimates for the homogeneous Sobolev seminorms $\dot H^σ$ of $ψ(\cdot,t)$, with at most exponential growth on $[0,T]$, together with estimates for $P_{\pm}N(ψ(\cdot,t),u(\cdot,t))$. Combining these bounds with the homogeneous and inhomogeneous Strichartz estimates for the Schrödinger system, we obtain, for $n\geq 3$ and every sharp Schrödinger admissible pair $(q,p)$, an a priori Strichartz-type estimate for $ψ$ in $L_T^q\dot W_x^{σ,p}$, expressed in terms of the initial datum $ψ(\cdot,0)$ and the a priori controls of $ψ$ in $L_T^\infty H_x^{σ+1}$ and $L_T^\infty L_x^\infty$.

☆ Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier
The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $σ: \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $Λ$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in Λ} \|σ_i -σ_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $σ_{|\partial Λ}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main Hölder regularity statement in a large domain $Λ\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $σ$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the Hölder regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $σ\in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial Λ}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.

Building on our previous results on propagation direction and the classification of traveling waves, we derive explicit Gaussian integral representations of both critical parameters, without involving unknown traveling-wave profiles or speeds. These formulas provide exact characterizations of the optimal competition parameters separating the corresponding propagation regimes. The derivation of these representations was assisted by ChatGPT (OpenAI) Pro, while the underlying theoretical foundations were established in our earlier works.
