This paper is concerned with space inhomogeneous Fermi-Dirac-Fokker-Planck equation posed on a classical kinetic phase space. The nonlinear factor $f(1-f)$ appears both in the transport term and in the collison part of the Fokker-Planck operator, accounting for the exclusion principle of fermions. Solutions are subject to the physical constraint $0\leq f\leq 1$. Previous existing results have mainly been obtained under suitable smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. A main difficulty stems from the nonlinear and degenerate parabolic structure of the equation. We prove the existence and uniqueness of global solutions without any smallness or close-to-equilibrium assumptions. To construct solutions, we use a vanishing viscosity approximation by adding a Laplacian in the spatial variable. We derive uniform estimates for the regularized problem and obtain compactness in the space of functions of bounded variation $(BV),$ allowing us to pass to the limit as the spatial viscosity vanishes. Since the limiting equation is degenerate with a nonlinear transport, we formulate an appropriate notion of entropy solutions incorporating the kinetic structure of the equation. We prove uniqueness within this class and show that every vanishing-viscosity limit satisfies the entropy formulation. Our result provides a global well-posedness theory beyond the perturbative regime.

We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

Let $p>1$ and $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded smooth domain. We study the following overdetermined problem for the p-Laplacian: \begin{equation*} \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δ_p u=f(x)&x\inΩ,\\ u=0&x\in\partialΩ,\\ \frac{\partial u}{\partialν}=g(x)&x\in\partialΩ, \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} where $ν$ is the inward unit normal to $\partialΩ$ and both data may depend on position. A boundary-local version of the moving-plane argument is developed for the possibly degenerate p-Laplace operator. The advantage of this argument is that it avoids the analysis of the degenerate set of the p-Laplacian. Under some reasonable structural conditions, we prove that the solvability of the above mentioned problem forces the domain to be a ball, the source to be radial, and the Neumann datum to be a suitable constant. We also give an explicit formula for the solution. Further consequences include one directional domain symmetry, the conclusion that full rigidity follows from reflection information in any set of directions whose linear reflections generate a dense subgroup of the orthogonal group $O(n)$, and a constant mean curvature characterization.

We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_θ$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

♻ ☆ Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster
We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. Consequently, its failure permits unbounded solution growth and we elucidate that connection through properties of $S(t)$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and provide an associated resonance taxonomy. The growth rate of ~$||(A-λI)^{-1}||_H$ on ~$i\R$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$, and, for rapid growth in $λ$, that gap can be infinite. In this case, we demonstrate implications for periodic solvability, and a mechanism for constructing smooth resonant forces. The theory developed here is motivated by (and demonstrated for) a hyperbolic-parabolic system, where the latter component provides the only system dissipation. Such dynamics are a simplification of fluid-structure phenomena, which demonstrate strong stability but do not provide unconditional periodic well-posedness. Though point-spectral resonance is ruled out, we note that $\mathcal R(I-S(T))\neq H$. Our main result here shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, a classical heat-wave system possesses periods $T$ which yield infinite derivative loss and, via supporting results, yield resonance with smooth forcing.

♻ ☆ Bouncing-ball modes in ergodic billiards
Zhenhao Li, Maciej Zworski
We show that for a horizontally stretched Bunimovich billiard, for almost every stretching parameter, there exists a sequence of eigenfunctions concentrating in the rectangular part. Thanks to the work of Markarian--Oliffson Kamphorst--Pinto de Carvalho, we know that for an open set of parameters such billiards are ergodic. The proof is a result of interaction with ChatGPT 6: we were curious if it could establish the existence of bouncing ball modes for Bunimovich or Sinai billiards. That was not successful until we suggested varying the wings. That produced an essentially complete argument for the existence of quasimodes. We then suggested using Hassell's parameter-variation argument which led to the result about eigenfunctions. The argument was then significantly simplified and clarified by the authors.

In this paper, we establish the existence of geometrically distinct bound states for the subcritical Nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation on a noncompact metric graph, provided that the mass is sufficiently large. By bound states we mean critical points of the NLS energy functional constrained to the manifold of fixed $L^2$-norm. We demonstrate that the NLS equation admits at least as many positive bound states as the number of bounded edges of the graph. Our approach is purely variational and relies on a doubly constrained minimization procedure. It is worth noting that, compared with the case where the potential vanishes, the scaling structure of solitons is destroyed here. Moreover, the classical energy asymptotic behavior $\mathcal{E}(φ_μ,\mathbb{R})=-θμ^{2β+1}$ is no longer preserved.
♻ ☆ The isoperimetric problem for four-dimensional parallelohedra

The honeycomb and Kelvin problems ask how space can be partitioned into cells of equal volume with the least surface area. We resolve this question in four dimensions for convex bodies that tile space by translations, showing that the regular $24$-cell uniquely minimizes surface area at fixed volume. We develop a framework combining an exact deficit identity, valid in every dimension, with a descent argument. As a consequence, the regular $24$-cell also minimizes surface area among such tiles containing a fixed ball.

This paper establishes the fully discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-regularity and the accompanying sharp maximal estimate for numerical approximations of parabolic stochastic partial differential equations. We consider the spatial finite element discretization $A_h$ of a general second-order elliptic operator $A=-\nabla \cdot a\nabla +b\cdot \nabla +c$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a smooth, bounded, convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, coupled with a broad class of temporal schemes, including rational approximations and the exponential Euler method. To obtain these optimal discrete regularity results, we establish a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the discrete spatial operator $A_h$, uniformly in the mesh size $h$. As a direct byproduct, we also establish the discrete-in-space stochastic maximal regularity for the corresponding spatial semi-discretizations. As an application, we establish the pathwise uniform convergence of a fully discrete approximation of the three-dimensional stochastic Allen--Cahn equation with variable diffusion coefficients and multiplicative noise.

♻ ☆ Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
Steven Flynn
We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $λ$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $λ$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.

Louis-Pierre Chaintron, Matteo Picco
A seminal work by Dacorogna and Moser introduced a way of constructing regular transport maps from a probability distribution on a bounded domain to another one. In this work, we extend this construction to the whole $\mathbb{R}^d$ for strictly asymptotically log-concave measures, a wide class of distributions that encompasses Lipschitz-perturbations of log-concave measures. We then leverage this construction to study geodesics in the space of probability measures on a product set with imposed marginal laws (couplings), for which we derive optimality conditions, answering an open question in a recent work by Conforti, Lacker and Pal. Taking inspiration from Brenier's variational model for incompressible fluids and its regularization, we further introduce an entropic regularization of the geodesic problem, which can be seen as the Schrödinger bridge problem on the space of couplings, for which we also derive optimality conditions. We eventually study convergence of minimizers as the regularization vanishes, and we prove convergence of the related Lagrange multipliers. Our approach involves proving uniform-in-time global regularity estimates on elliptic and parabolic equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$, by exploiting the structure of asymptotically log-concave measures using the probabilistic notion of reflection coupling.

We study the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for a class of hyperbolic quasilinear evolution systems with fractional dissipation and commutators of the fractional Laplacian $(-Δ)^α$ with $α\in(0,1)$. The analysis is motivated by the compressible isentropic Navier-Stokes equations with fractional diffusion and the compressible Euler alignment system with singular communication weights. We show that the contribution of the commutators to the energy is absorbed by the dissipation. Our approach does not rely on the cancellation condition previously used to recover the coercivity of the highest-order non-local terms. We further show that the commutator term induces a loss of regularity in the stability estimates, preventing the standard contraction argument from being applied. Therefore, we instead establish the relative compactness of the solution operator and apply Schauder's fixed point theorem. The resulting theory provides local existence for arbitrary orders $α\in(0,1)$ and identifies the obstacles to local uniqueness in the presence of fractional commutators.

It has been observed that the dynamics of the Toda lattice can be well described by solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation in the continuum limit. We show that, under the KdV scaling and a suitable translation, the solution of the Toda lattice with H^1 initial data converges to that of the KdV equation globally in time. Our proof relies on tools from harmonic analysis and also on the construction and the conservation of mass and energy of the Toda lattice, the latter of which are derived from the completely integrable structure of the Toda lattice. As a consequence, we obtain long-wave KdV limits for the Toda lattice.

Under a Hölder-type decay assumption on $ f $, we derive sharp boundary $C^{1,β'}$ estimates with an explicit exponent, and establish a quantitative non-degeneracy estimate in the singular region. Using the Daleckii-Krein formula, we relate radial convexity to the positivity of the Hadamard square of the corresponding Loewner matrix. This leads us to conjecture that radial convexity of order $n$ is equivalent to matrix monotonicity of degree $n$, and we prove this equivalence in degree $2$. ☆ Absolutely minimising Lipschitz extensions between Hilbert spaces
Krzysztof J. Ciosmak
Every Lipschitz map from a closed subset of a real Hilbert space into a real Hilbert space has an absolutely minimising Lipschitz extension: an extension whose Lipschitz constant on every open subset of the complement, bounded or not, equals the Lipschitz constant of its restriction to the boundary of that subset. Neither space need be separable. This answers a question of Naor and Sheffield. For targets of dimension at least two we prove a density theorem on connected domains: every optimal extension of a boundary datum can be approximated, uniformly on compact sets, by extensions whose Lipschitz constant on every nonempty open subset, and on its boundary, equals the constant of the datum. Consequently, in contrast with the scalar case, such a datum has a unique absolutely minimising extension exactly when its optimal extension is unique, and absolutely minimising extensions need not be closed under uniform convergence, even for fixed smooth data on a planar disk. The extensions are built by finite piecewise isometric interpolation: on nested polyhedra with dense union they are piecewise affine and preserve distances in at least two directions on each simplex, a structure described through leaves of 1-Lipschitz maps. The boundary constraints are handled by a midpoint argument for admissible values, and a Kuratowski-Zorn argument removes the separability assumption while preserving previously prescribed values. We also characterise the bounded linear maps that are absolutely minimising extensions of all data determining their operator norm.

Then $\dim\operatorname{span}\{f,g,h\}\leq1$ if either $\operatorname{deg} P\geq 4$ and the boundary spectrum of $θ$ has logarithmic capacity zero, or $\operatorname{deg} P = 3$ and the boundary spectrum contains at most one point. This settles new cases of a problem of Dyakonov, subsumes the previously known results, and recovers the classical fact that polynomial parametrizations of a smooth projective plane curve of degree at least three are projectively constant.

Moreover, through a semiclassical analysis of the density generated by normalized Dirichlet eigenfunctions, we establish the collective asymptotic behaviors of the quantities appearing in the inequality in various regimes. These semiclassical behaviors show that the rank-dependent term $N-1$ on the right-hand side is indispensable.

Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(λ\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.

♻ ☆ Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
Boris Muha, Sebastian Schwarzacher, Justin T. Webster
We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. Consequently, its failure permits unbounded solution growth and we elucidate that connection through properties of $S(t)$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and provide an associated resonance taxonomy. The growth rate of ~$||(A-λI)^{-1}||_H$ on ~$i\R$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$, and, for rapid growth in $λ$, that gap can be infinite. In this case, we demonstrate implications for periodic solvability, and a mechanism for constructing smooth resonant forces. The theory developed here is motivated by (and demonstrated for) a hyperbolic-parabolic system, where the latter component provides the only system dissipation. Such dynamics are a simplification of fluid-structure phenomena, which demonstrate strong stability but do not provide unconditional periodic well-posedness. Though point-spectral resonance is ruled out, we note that $\mathcal R(I-S(T))\neq H$. Our main result here shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, a classical heat-wave system possesses periods $T$ which yield infinite derivative loss and, via supporting results, yield resonance with smooth forcing.

A $C^*$-category is to a $C^*$-algebra what a groupoid is to a group. An example is the category of Hilbert spaces and bounded linear maps, and indeed, every $C^*$-category can be represented as a sub-$*$-category of this. Analogously, a $W^*$-category is a $C^*$-category where every object has a predual, and we might expect a representation theory on Hilbert spaces where the resulting morphism spaces are $σ$-weakly closed. We identify a gap in the literature here, stemming from the (perhaps surprising) fact that a $C^*$-algebra can have a non-isometric predual and yet not be a $W^*$-algebra. Using the theory of dual TROs (ternary rings of operators) we repair this gap, and along the way, also give further justification to arguments in the literature about dual TROs. Motivated by the theory of Dual Banach Algebras, we offer an alternative axiomatisation of $W^*$-categories where we allow non-isometric preduals of the hom spaces, but require that they are additionally bimodules in a certain sense. This involves the theory of self-dual Hilbert $C^*$-modules.

♻ ☆ Constructive Peter--Weyl Theory: What Is Known and What Remains Open
Takao Inoué
What is known about constructive Peter-Weyl theory, and what remains open? This expository article separates established theorems, comparisons between formulations, and questions requiring further investigation in the Bishop-Coquand-Spitters line. Its central finding is that constructive Peter-Weyl theory already has an established compact-group approximation core: under specified analytic and Gelfand hypotheses, finite-rank central convolution projections converge strongly in the Haar L2 norm. We make these hypotheses and the projection-kernel normalization explicit, and record the resulting spectral Hilbert completion. This answers the question of completion affirmatively for that precise core theorem. Broader claims about the whole classical package or its validity across constructive foundations require separate comparisons; uniform approximation, irreducible representation data, and point-set recovery are not inferred from strong convergence alone. The historical problems of left-right almost periodicity and universal Bohr compactification are examined with a dated follow-up literature review, distinguishing related progress from a verified resolution. A sufficient metric realization criterion, finite examples, and a separate nonassociative outlook clarify the scope of the established method. An extended appendix proves the classical Peter-Weyl theorem through Haar averaging, convolution, spectral density, point separation, and irreducible orthogonality. Stage-by-stage comparisons explain which arguments transfer constructively and which require additional data or a different proof. The article therefore identifies what is proved and what additional statements or data remain to be examined, without treating an unidentified resolution as proof that a problem is currently open.

Under mild assumptions on the weights, we characterize the weighted frame vectors and weighted Parseval frame vectors, that is, those vectors $ξ$ for which $\{a_α\mathbf{T}^αξ\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ is a frame or a Parseval frame. We reduce the problem to characterizing surjective module maps from the reproducing analytic Hilbert module associated with the weights onto the module $\mathcal{K}$, equipped with the module structure defined by $\mathbf{T}$. It is shown that weighted Parseval frame vectors differ by a unimodular scalar whenever they exist. If the kernel defined by the weights has the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property, then any two associated weighted frame vectors are similar whenever they exist. We also focus on the case of the Hardy kernel on the polydisc, that is, the case $a_α=1$ for all $α\in\mathbb{Z}^n_+$. This is related to the famous Douglas--Foias problem: whether two similar quotient modules of the Hardy spaces $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)~(n>1)$ are equal. Our result shows that the answer is negative. This leads to the conclusion that frame vectors for representations of $\mathbb{Z}_+^n$ $(n>1)$ may fail to be similar. It means that, for the case $a_α=1$, there exists a tuple $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\dots,T_n)$ with $n>1$ on $\mathcal{K}$ and two distinct frame vectors for $\mathbf{T}$ which are not similar.

A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.

We prove an explicit lower spectral bound for independent random vectors with prescribed group multiplicities. Let $v_{ij}\in\mathbb C^d$, $1\le i\le l$, $1\le j\le k_i$, be independent random vectors with finite support and $\mathbb E v_{ij}v_{ij}^*=A_i$, where $\sum_{i=1}^l A_i=I_d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(A_i)\geε$. Set $k=\max_i k_i$, $n=\max_i\operatorname{rank}(A_i)$, and $K=\sum_{i=1}^l k_i$. If $n>(6+4\sqrt2)k$ and $2\sqrt{nk}-k<ε\le n/2$, then, with positive probability, \[ λ_K\left(\sum_{i=1}^l\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}v_{ij}v_{ij}^*\right) \ge n-(\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{n-ε})^2. \] As a consequence, we obtain a restricted invertibility result selecting exactly $k_i$ vectors from the $i$th group of a Parseval frame. The proof combines interlacing families, a reciprocal transformation of mixed characteristic polynomials, and a multivariate barrier estimate that accommodates repeated differentiation in the same variable.

We study isomorphic embeddings into Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces \(\ell_Φ\), where the normalized generating sequence \(Φ=\{φ_n\}\) satisfies the \(δ_2\) condition. Using admissible normalized blocks, we construct an associated limiting family \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) of Orlicz functions. If a Banach space \(X\) with a symmetric basis embeds into \(\ell_Φ\), then there is a function \(ψ\in\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) such that the basis of \(X\) is equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_ψ\). An Orlicz sequence space \(\ell_ψ\) embeds if and only if \(ψ\) is equivalent near zero to a member of \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\); in particular, \(\ell^p\) embeds exactly when such a member is equivalent to \(t^p\). Assuming differentiability of the generators on a common interval near zero, we also derive the necessary bound \(p\leq b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\), where the upper growth index incorporates the summable errors in the \(δ_2\) condition. The same index yields cotype \(q\) for every \(q\geq2\) with \(q>b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\). Examples with nonuniform growth and lacunary weights illustrate this bound. For alternating Nakano exponents, the explicit limiting family gives a sharper restriction than the index alone. For general Nakano exponents, we recover the known exact cotype criterion, including attainment of the optimal exponent. For weighted Orlicz spaces, we express the cotype criterion through summable scalar errors and recover the formula using the global upper growth index when \(w\in\mathcal A\).

Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.

Anderson Barbosa, Daniel Núñez-Alarcón, Daniel Pellegrino, Anselmo Raposo
The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality states that, for a $d$-homogeneous polynomial $P:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb C$, $P(z)=\sum_{|α|=d}c_αz^α$, the coefficient norm $(\sum_{|α|=d}|c_α|^{p_d})^{1/p_d}$ is bounded by $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}\|P\|_\infty$, where $p_d=2d/(d+1)$ and $B_d^{\mathrm{pol}}$ is independent of $N$. Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the supremum norm on the unit polydisc. This inequality has a Boolean analogue for the Fourier--Walsh coefficients of functions of degree at most $d$, with the supremum taken over $\{-1,1\}^N$. In this setting, Defant, Mastyło and Pérez obtained subexponential bounds, and Ivanisvili established polynomial growth. Further polynomial estimates were obtained by Slote, Tseng and Volberg in the Boolean setting and by Slote and Volberg for cyclic groups. We study these coefficient inequalities in a broader framework of finite systems of functions that encompasses and extends the Boolean and cyclic settings. This framework also admits a natural $\ell_p$ formulation, leading to Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. For orthonormal systems, we obtain polynomial bounds for the Bohnenblust--Hille constants and, for sufficiently large $p$, for the constants in these Hardy--Littlewood-type inequalities. In the Boolean case, the polynomial power is $5/2$, with a cubic logarithmic factor.

We study the numerical radius \(ω(T)\) of a bounded linear operator \(T\) on a complex Hilbert space. Write \(T=A+iB\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are the real and imaginary parts of \(T\). A central result is the exact formula \[ ω(T)=\fracπ{2}\sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left|\left\langle (A\cos πt+B\sin πt)x,x\right\rangle\right|\,dt . \] For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), we also prove the power form \[ ω^{2n}(T)=\frac{4^n}{\binom{2n}{n}} \sup_{\|x\|=1}\int_0^1 \left\langle (A\cos πt+B\sin πt)x,x\right\rangle^{2n}\,dt . \] This yields sharp upper bounds; for \(n=1\), together with the matching integral lower bound, it recovers Kittaneh's classical two-sided inequality \[ \frac14\|T^*T+TT^*\|\le ω^2(T)\le \frac12\|T^*T+TT^*\|. \] Furthermore, we obtain exact numerical radius formulas for some block operator matrices, including a \(3\times3\) nilpotent matrix and longer alternating paths. The factor \(π/2\) is best possible.

For what sequences does the condition $$ \lim_{i\to \infty} \sup_{f_i\in F_i} \|Tf_i\|_Y=0 $$ hold for every Banach space $Y$ and every compact operator $T:X\to Y$? We illustrate the applicability of the criteria by examples from the literature and by characterizing the $L^p\to L^p$ compactness of dyadic paraproducts on general measure spaces through introducing a space of vanishing mean oscillations with respect to mass (as opposed to length) of cubes.

♻ ☆ Inverse-Limit Detection Envelopes as Calkin Algebras

For a unital Banach algebra $A$ with $\|1_A\|=1$ and a decreasing sequence $(I_r)$ of proper closed two-sided ideals of finite codimension, we introduce the bounded detection envelope $$\widehat A:=\operatorname{Env}^{b}_{(I_r)}(A)=\varprojlim^{b}(A/I_r,π_r^s),\qquad \|(a_r)_r\|=\sup_r\|a_r\|.$$ Combining vector-valued Bourgain--Delbaen extensions, oracle Turing-machine recursion, and Argyros--Haydon operator analysis, we construct a separable Banach space $X$ such that, isometrically as unital Banach algebras, $$\operatorname{Cal}(X)=\mathcal{B}(X)/\mathcal{K}(X)\simeq\widehat A. $$ We also characterize these envelopes as the unital Banach algebras with norm-one units admitting an isometric predual and countably many jointly faithful weak-star-to-norm continuous finite-dimensional unital representations. These include incidence algebras, $\ell_\infty$, and the unitization of Tsirelson's original space. Further applications concern analytic operator algebras, Fourier--Stieltjes and Fourier multiplier algebras of countable discrete groups, and classical and quantum convolution algebras. In particular, we realize $H^\infty(\mathbb D)$, $\operatorname{Mult}(H_2^2)$, $\mathcal L_2$, $M_{\mathrm{cb}}A(\mathbb F_2)$, and $C^u(O_3^+)^*$ as Calkin algebras, with their canonical norms and products.

For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every separable Banach space $V$, we use an oracle-relative two-sorted finite-extension construction, whose oracle records the local rational structure of $V$, to construct a separable Banach space $X_V$ such that $$ \operatorname{Cal}(X_V)=\mathcal{B}(X_V)/\mathcal{K}(X_V)\simeq \begin{pmatrix} \mathbb{K}&0\\ V^*&\mathbb{K} \end{pmatrix} $$ as Banach algebras. The identification of $V^*$ with the Jacobson radical is isometric. Consequently, every nonzero dual Banach space with a separable predual admits, after an equivalent renorming, a unital Banach-algebra structure isomorphic to the Calkin algebra of a separable Banach space. Moreover, there is a separable Banach space $X$ such that every separable Banach space is isometric to $\mathcal{J}/\mathcal{K}(X)$ for a closed two-sided ideal $\mathcal{J}$ of $\mathcal{B}(X)$, and the subspace--ideal correspondence preserves the canonical order.

For a $C^*$-algebra $A$ let $\mathcal I(A)$ be the set of all elements $a+b$ with $a,b\in A_+$, $ab=0$ and $\|a\|=\|b\|=1$. We study the algebraic, metric and topological properties of $\mathcal I(A)$. We describe $\mathcal I(A\oplus B)$ and show that $\mathcal I(A/J)\subseteqπ(\mathcal I(A))$ for the quotient map $π:A\to A/J$. For finite-dimensional $A$ we prove $\mathcal I(A)=\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E(A))$, where $E(A)$ is the set of minimal projections of $A$ and $\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E)$ is the set of positive norm-one elements at distance one from every element of $E$; we also show that the analogous statement with the minimal projections of the bidual fails in general. When $\mathcal I(A)\neq\varnothing$ the distance from $1$ to $\mathcal I(A)$ is $0$ or $1$, according to whether $A$ has a nontrivial projection. Moreover, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm compact if and only if $A$ is finite-dimensional, closedness of $\mathcal I(A)$ passes to hereditary subalgebras, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm closed for every von Neumann algebra, and the extreme points of $\mathcal I(A)$ are exactly its projections. For a compact, locally path connected space $X$ the set $\mathcal I(C(X))$ is closed, whereas $\mathcal I(\ell_c(A))$ fails to be closed when $A$ is unital without nontrivial projections.

On the other hand $ZDRR(C(X\times[0,1]))=0$ for every compact Hausdorff space $X$, so $ZDRR$ and $RR$ can differ arbitrarily.

☆ A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra

We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $\varphi\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{it\varphi}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_\varphi\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_\varphi)$, where $c_\varphi>0$ and $T_\varphi>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.
☆ Dimensional transition and spectral instability in lattice Hardy inequalities
Carlos Lizama
Discretization can change a sharp stability threshold even when the continuum threshold is recovered at infinity. We study this phenomenon for the Hardy inequality on the integer lattice in dimensions at least three: its best coefficient agrees with the continuum value through dimension eight and is smaller from dimension nine onwards. We characterize this transition by the total critical defect, the summable error obtained by testing the lattice operator against the critical continuum power. A theta-function representation proves that the defect is negative and strictly decreasing from dimension nine; explicit positive Hardy remainders establish its positivity in dimensions three through eight. An exact energy identity relates this defect to the energy saved by optimizing the profile outside the neighbours of the origin. This exterior remains stable in dimensions eight and nine, locating the first loss of positivity in its coupling to those neighbours. We give self-contained proofs of both dimensional ranges. We then describe how local attraction creates a negative eigenvalue in a general class of lattice operators with critical inverse-square tails. Its magnitude is exponentially small near the threshold, with both the rate and the multiplicative prefactor determined by zero-energy solutions. The result allows connected finite modifications of the lattice and nonradial corrections to the tail. The same analysis controls the spread of the emerging state and gives a two-dimensional return scale for the associated Markov chain in every ambient dimension.

☆ Splines and Operators: Part II - Resolution of Inverse Problems
Michael Unser
We present a unified treatment of the data-fitting problems with quadratic (Hilbertian) regularization that arise in approximation theory, machine learning, engineering, and statistics. The generic problem is an optimization in the continuum: given $M$ linear measurements of an unknown function, one minimizes a convex data-fidelity term that is penalized by $\|\mathrm{L} f\|^2_{L_2}$, where $\mathrm{L} $ is a differential-like (spline-admissible) operator. The natural domain of the minimization is the native space $\mathcal{H}_\mathrm{L}$ of $\mathrm{L} $ - the largest Hilbert space over which the regularizer remains meaningful - for which we provide a concise and directly usable characterization. Central to our formulation is a measurement-adapted (conditioned) basis that decouples the null-space and spline components of the solution. This basis serves in three places. First, it tightens the formulation of our representer theorem, which confines the unique solution to an $M$-dimensional space without any orthogonality constraint on the coefficients. Second, it streamlines the implementation, as the exact discretization of the problem becomes an unconstrained convex program with closed-form solutions in the least-squares case, which covers ridge regression, Tikhonov regularization, and smoothing splines. Third, it makes the bridge with the minimum-mean-square-error estimation of generalized Gaussian processes, which is the topic of a companion paper.
☆ Splines and Operators: Part I - Admissibility and Native Spaces
Michael Unser
The variational theory of splines requires a native space: a Hilbert space over which the regularization energy $\|\mathrm{L} f\|_{L_2}^2$ is well defined and the minimum-energy interpolation problem admits a spline solution. In this paper, we characterize the operators $\mathrm{L}$ that enable the construction of such spaces. Our framework is based on the completion of a space $\mathcal{S}$ of test functions in a controlled Gelfand-triple configuration $\mathcal{S}\subset\mathcal{H}\subset\mathcal{S}'$, which we call a Hilbert-Gelfand space. This departs from the classical reproducing-kernel techniques. Our construction is substantially more general, as it supports arbitrary linear operators and singular behaviors, and it recovers the reproducing-kernel setting as a particular case. It is also complete and canonical: the admissibility conditions on $\mathrm{L}$ are necessary and sufficient, and $\mathrm{L}$ determines its native space as the unique Hilbert-Gelfand space on which it extends to a bounded surjection onto $L_2$. We first show that Hilbert-Gelfand spaces are in one-to-one correspondence with compatible Riesz pairs $(\mathrm{A},\mathrm{A}^{-1})$ of positive-definite operators $\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{S}'$. We then extend this correspondence to conditional Riesz pairs, where $\mathrm{A}$ is only conditionally positive-definite, which is the scenario that is relevant to splines. The theory identifies the \emph{attainable null space} of the energy as the unique admissible conditioning, realizes the abstract completions as concrete spaces of distributions, and provides a verifiable admissibility condition in terms of a dual energy functional. The framework is illustrated with the fractional Laplacian, which covers polyharmonic and thin-plate splines, and with ordinary differential operators, which cover exponential splines.

Jeffrey Humpherys
In the 2004 collection \emph{Unsolved Problems in Mathematical Systems and Control Theory}, Erik Verriest posed the problem of characterizing Riccati stability ``without invoking additional matrices.'' We give such a characterization through a scalar invariant of the resolvent family. The invariant is defined by covariance balances using at most $n^2+1$ frequency--direction pairs. A finite-dimensional separation argument shows that this covariance radius equals the optimal common ellipsoidal norm of the resolvent family. Combined with the strict bounded real lemma, this yields a necessary and sufficient condition for Riccati stability involving only the Hurwitz property of the first matrix and a single scalar inequality. The invariant reduces to the ordinary spectral radius for one matrix, lies between the pointwise spectral-radius and unscaled small-gain levels of the resolvent family, and coincides with the operator-space spectral radius of Shalit and Shamovich for the natural resolvent function space. The main results have been formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.
♻ ☆ Ideal structure of $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebras
Yeong Chyuan Chung, Xinhui Du
For a uniformly locally finite coarse space $(X,\mathcal E)$ and $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty]$, we classify the nonzero geometric ideals of the $\ell^p$ uniform Roe algebra $B_u^p(X,\mathcal E)$ by the ideals of $\mathcal E$, equivalently by ideals in the associated family of controlled partial coverings. Hence the geometric ideal lattice is canonically independent of $p$. For $p\in[1,\infty]$, we identify $B_u^p(X,\mathcal E)$ isometrically with the reduced $L^p$ operator algebra of the coarse groupoid and show that this identification preserves essential support, carrying geometric and ghostly ideals to dynamical and restrictive ideals. Under property A, controlled $p$-kernels yield a multiplier approximate identity with controlled propagation; consequently every ideal is geometric and every ghost is trivial. Thus the full ideal lattices are canonically independent of $p$ under property A. For $p\in\{0,1,\infty\}$, the complete ideal classification holds without property A; on the groupoid side, the corresponding unconditional conclusion holds for $p\in\{1,\infty\}$.
comment: 63 pages. Substantially revised and reorganized, with corrections to proofs, statements, and notation. The treatment of the extreme exponents, the non-unital case, and the groupoid ideal-support results has been clarified. Material on partial coverings and limit operators has been moved to appendices, with expanded proofs. Section 7 of v1 on Morita equivalence moved to arXiv:2608.30380
♻ ☆ Extendable Shift Maps and the Canonical Map on Generalized Countable Markov Shifts
Rodrigo Bissacot, Iván Diaz-Granados, Thiago Raszeja
We obtain an operator-algebraic characterization of when the shift map can be continuously extended from a standard countable Markov shift $Σ_A$ to its generalized countable Markov shift $X_A$, a compactification of $Σ_A$. We show that a canonical unital completely positive map on the Exel--Laca algebra $O_A$ can be defined exactly when the shift extends continuously from $Σ_A$ to $X_A$, and that in this case its restriction to the maximal commutative C$^*$-subalgebra $D_A$ is a $*$-endomorphism to which the extended shift is dual. We also give a criterion on the matrix $A$ itself, in terms of the convergence of its columns, and exhibit classes of transition matrices satisfying these equivalent conditions. Column-finiteness of $A$ is necessary for the existence of the continuous extension. Finally, we construct an example in which the set of empty words is a Cantor set and the extended dynamics on it is the inverse of the dyadic odometer.
comment: 46 pages, 19 figures. Submitted version
♻ ☆ Domains of Monomial Convergence in Banach Sequence Spaces
Zhouzhe Wang
A classical phenomenon distinguishing infinite-dimensional holomorphy from its finite-dimensional counterpart is that monomial expansions of holomorphic functions need not converge absolutely. In this paper, we systematically investigate monomial convergence on complex Banach sequence spaces. We establish general structural results and give a negative answer to Lempert's problem. We then determine the domains of absolute monomial convergence for holomorphic functions on the classical Banach sequence spaces and obtain a complete classification for continuous homogeneous polynomials. As a further application, we establish a sharp comparison between two notions of convergence radius for homogeneous Taylor expansions on $\ell^1$. The methods developed here are of independent interest and may be applied in other places.
♻ ☆ Algebraic Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem for quantum measurement
Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher
We establish an operational framework connecting the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold (KA) representation theorem to quantum information theory. By introducing and proving an algebraic, bounded-degree polynomial version of the theorem, we demonstrate that any target physical property of an unentangled multi-qubit product state can be exactly decomposed using a finite, fixed set of local ``inner'' observables and a shallow architecture of univariate polynomials. We further analyse the stability of this Quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold (QKA) representation under adversarial perturbations. In stark contrast to the pathological instabilities and severe reparameterisation sensitivities inherent to the classical Kolmogorov--Arnold representation theorem, our algebraic quantum framework exhibits remarkable resilience. We prove that the representation remains stable against bounded physical perturbations acting on the inner measurement operators, and show via the Heisenberg picture that it is inherently immune to adversarial quantum channel attacks acting on the input states.

☆ A Riesz-Map Preconditioned Extragradient Method for Price Formation in Mean Field Games
Yeva Gevorgyan, Diogo Gomes
We develop and analyze a projected extragradient method, preconditioned by a Riesz map, for a first-order price-formation mean field game in one space dimension. The model couples Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and transport equations through a global market-clearing constraint. Finite propagation justifies truncating the first-order transport equation to a bounded interval. A monotone weak formulation incorporates the mixed initial--terminal data. Its Riesz map uses $L^2$ norms for density and price directions and a space-time $H^1$ norm for value-function directions, preconditioning the residual without adding higher-order regularization terms to the MFG equations. A density-only argument rules out cocoercivity on the localized admissible set in every equivalent Hilbert metric, motivating extragradient updates. For $H(x,p)=p^2/2$, we use a monotone upwind discretization with adjoint-consistent transport and a state-constraint boundary closure. We establish a mesh-independent Lipschitz bound on bounded convex admissible sets with uniform density, slope, and price bounds. With exact metric projection onto these sets, the iteration converges to a solution of the discrete variational inequality on each fixed grid, with an admissible step-size threshold independent of both mesh sizes. Convergence under mesh refinement is not proved. On a quadratic benchmark, all reported runs reach the stopping tolerance with one fixed step size across a factor-of-16 reduction in both mesh sizes. Price errors and value-function errors measured away from low-density regions decay approximately at first order under refinement, while density errors decrease more slowly.

☆ An Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients
Amĺie Loher, Connor Mooney, Clément Mouhot, Lukas Niebel, Luis Silvestre, Yuzhe Zhu
We give an exposition of a proof, discovered by Astra, of an Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients. We explain this method in the simpler elliptic and parabolic settings as well.

☆ The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
Gianmarco Giovannardi, Simone Verzellesi
In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.
☆ The Inviscid Limit in Uniformly Local Yudovich Spaces
Zachary Radke
We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes and Euler equations with the velocity in $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and the vorticity in the uniformly local Yudovich space $Y^θ_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $θ$ grows sufficiently slowly, then for every $T>0$, solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation converge to solutions of the Euler equation in $L^{\infty}([0,T];L^2_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ as $ν\to 0^+$, provided they are generated from the same initial data.
comment: 25 pages
☆ Ground states and sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for logarithmic Schrödinger equations with partial confinement
Baihong Li, Jarosław Mederski, Xiangjian Zeng
We study the logarithmic Schrödinger equation with an arbitrary positive semidefinite quadratic potential and a periodic potential in the unconfined directions. The main variational difficulty is to turn a constrained minimizer into a critical point when the energy is extended-valued and not of class $C^1$ on the natural Hilbert space. We establish an abstract principle for convex lower semicontinuous energies with a smooth perturbation, allowing a scaling law for the full energy without requiring homogeneity of its convex part. Combined with a profile decomposition under integer translations, this principle yields a positive ground state for every rank of the quadratic form. When the periodic potential vanishes, we prove a sharp anisotropic logarithmic Sobolev inequality, determine its optimal constant and all equality cases, and classify positive ground states as explicit anisotropic Gaussons, unique up to translations along the kernel of the quadratic form. When the periodic component is constant, we also establish existence and classify all normalized ground states at every prescribed positive mass, with explicit formulas for the minimum energy and the associated Lagrange multiplier.
☆ Existence and large-field asymptotics of Hopfions in a continuum model of frustrated magnets
Glal Bacho, Christof Melcher
We study a continuum model of frustrated magnetism that supports particle-like field configurations with nontrivial Hopf index. The energy functional combines competing second and first order exchange interactions with a stabilizing external magnetic field and gives rise to a variational problem for maps from three-dimensional space into the two-sphere. We prove the existence of energy minimizers in infinitely many nontrivial homotopy classes. We further establish the existence of a unit-charge Hopfion in the regime of strong external fields. Finally, we analyze the corresponding large-field limit, identify the natural concentration scale, and prove strong convergence of suitably rescaled minimizers to a minimizer of a limiting variational problem.
☆ Characterizing higher-dimensional Hölder domains via spherical geometric functions
Emily Casey, Max Engelstein, Tatiana Toro
In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has Hölder decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,β}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold. Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $β$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.
comment: 32 pages, 9 figures; no use of AI (except to make pictures)
☆ Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
Valentino Badalucco
Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.
comment: 85 pages, 2 figures, 3 appendices
☆ Scattering for the KP-II equation
Xi Chen
We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the KP-II equation with localized initial data. The hypotheses cover all Schwartz functions, data with a half spatial moment in $B^2_{1,1}$, and a class of weighted tensor Besov spaces allowing low regularity in either coordinate. The proof uses the scalar $\bar\partial$ equation associated with the heat operator. A uniform inverse estimate and an exact $L^2$ identity give an inverse construction for large amplitudes. We then estimate the nonlinear remainder on the propagation cones of free solutions and identify the limiting spectral mass through the heat equation. No smallness or zero horizontal mean condition is required. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum.
☆ Asymmetric minimal mass blow-up for the quintic NLS on a star graph
Mattia Buratti, François Genoud, Vladimir Georgiev
This work is concerned with the focusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a star graph with two edges, with a delta interaction of arbitrary strength at the vertex. We construct a non-radial, minimal mass, finite time blow-up solution, whose singularity forms at an arbitrarily prescribed interior point of one edge. Our approach is based on a suitable cut-off of the standard pseudoconformal blow-up solution of the focusing quintic NLS on the line, inspired by Ogawa-Tsutsumi and Burq-Gérard-Tzvetkov. A noteworthy feature of our construction is the persistence of the domain of the Hamiltonian under the flow, obtained by the persistence of regularity method of Kato. We also identify a two-parameter family of distinct blow-up profiles, which should play a central role in the classification of non-radial minimal mass blow-up solutions on the star graph. Our construction is generic and can be extended to a star graph with an arbitrary number of edges. It can certainly also be adapted to other types of metric graphs.
comment: 22 pages, 1 figure
☆ Travel time tomography for elliptically anisotropic elastic planar media
Joonas Ilmavirta, Teemu Saksala, Hjørdis Schlüter
We study the gauge of the travel time tomography problem for elliptically anisotropic planar media. Under this assumption the respective slowness surfaces consist of an inner ellipse and an outer circle. Hence, the singularities of seismic waves propagate on geodesics given by two Riemannian metrics of which the one related to shear waves is conformally Euclidean. We show that if both of these metrics are lens rigid then, up to boundary fixing diffeomorphisms, each elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensor is uniquely determined by the lens data whenever it has at least one isotropic point. If none of those points exists, then there are exactly two elliptically anisotropic stiffness tensors with the same lens data. Clearly, not all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms preserve the imposed structure of the slowness surface. We show that the set of well-behaved diffeomorphisms is never a subgroup of all boundary fixing diffeomorphisms. Our proofs are based on an interplay of algebra and geometry, and the key of the proofs is a characterization of the elliptic anisotropy via several polynomial conditions.
☆ Topping's conjecture for solutions of harmonic map flow with isolated bubbles
Melanie Rupflin, Alex Waldron, Sebastian Woodward
By establishing a weighted Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality for maps which are close to a fixed harmonic map modulo scaling, we prove Topping's conjecture on continuity of the body map in the case of finite time singularities at which only isolated bubbles form.
comment: 8 pages
☆ Sharp upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products
Jade Brisson, Bruno Colbois, Alexandre Girouard, Katie Gittins, Jean Lagacé-Taylor
We obtain sharp isoperimetric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products whose bases are compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary and whose fibres are closed Riemannian manifolds. These bounds involve the volume of the warped product and of its boundary, as well as the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on the fibre and the Steklov eigenvalues of the base. After separation of variables, these bounds are obtained by comparison with auxiliary Helmholtz-Steklov problems on the base involving weighted Laplace operators naturally induced by the warping function. We also study the effect of various natural geometric constraints, such as the warping function being identically equal to one on the boundary. The proofs make use of various spectral approximation methods, including homogenisation on manifolds when the fibres are one-dimensional.
comment: This work supersedes arXiv:2512.15416 where upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues on warped products were obtained for the case where the fibre has dimension at least two. By using different techniques, this work treats the case where fibres have any dimension (including dimension one) and obtains sharp bounds
☆ Diffraction of waves by finite thin coatings: asymptotic expansion and effective models
Cédric Baudet
We consider the Helmholtz equation in a Dirichlet angular sector (which may be locally perturbed) covered on one side by a thin homogeneous layer. First, we propose an asymptotic expansion of the solution at any order and for any angle when the thickness of the layer tends to 0, using a matched asymptotic expansion. This consists in introducing different asymptotic expansions in three subdomains -- the vicinity of the corner, the layer and the rest of the domain -- that are linked through matching conditions. The presence of the corner makes these matching conditions delicate to derive because the fields have complex singular behaviors. We overcome this difficulty using a novel system of algebraic tools, including formal series and operators on these series. Moreover, we justify the asymptotic expansion with error estimates and provide details on the form of the expansion depending on the angle. We numerically validate this expansion up to order 5. This requires computing the behavior at infinity of some corner profiles. To do this, we introduce a Galerkin-type method enriched by complements at infinity. These complements are known functions that appear in the behavior at infinity of the corner profiles with coefficients that become unknowns of the system. Finally, we propose effective models of order 3, resp. 5 where, far from the corner, the layer is replaced with an effective Robin, resp. Ventcel, boundary condition and, near the corner, an artificial boundary is introduced and a Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) type condition is imposed. The DtN map relies on a modal decomposition of the truncated asymptotic expansion at order 3, resp. 5. The modes take into account the singular behavior of the expansion terms, the corner profiles and some algebraic matching coefficients. We prove the well-posedness of our effective models, as well as error estimates, and provide numerical results.
comment: PhD thesis, 288 pages, 55 figures
☆ Statistical inference for rough Burgers-type stochastic partial differential equations
Simon Chony Acosta Christian Olivera Ciprian Tudor
We consider the Burgers-type stochastic PDE \[ du = θ\,\partial_x^2 u\,dt + f(u)\,dt + g(u)\,\partial_x u\,dt + σ\,dW(t), \] driven by space--time white noise on the one-dimensional torus, where \(θ>0\) is the diffusivity parameter and \(σ>0\) the noise intensity. The transport term \(g(u)\,\partial_x u\) admits no classical interpretation, and we work with the mild solutions defined via rough paths following~\cite{Hairer2011}, for which the solution decomposes as \(u=ψ+R\) with \(ψ\) a stationary centred Gaussian process solving a damped stochastic heat equation and \(R\) a remainder. We first show that, away from the initial time, \(R\) is Lipschitz in space and Hölder in time of order strictly greater than \(1/2\), hence strictly smoother than \(ψ\) in both variables. We then compute exactly the spatial quadratic variation and the temporal quartic variation of \(ψ\), almost surely and not merely in \(L^{2}(Ω)\), and prove that the corresponding variations of \(u\) are unaffected by the remainder. Combined with an exact time-scaling identity, this separation of regularity scales yields strongly consistent pathwise estimators of \(θ\). To our knowledge this is the first inference procedure for an SPDE whose solution is defined only pathwise, as a measurable function of a rough path, rather than as an Itô process.
☆ An inverse spectral problem for the wave equation with a varying Robin parameter at the boundary
Antti Hannukainen, Petr Kulikov, Matti Lassas, Lauri Oksanen
An inverse spectral problem for a $(1+1)$-dimensional wave equation with wave speed $c(x)$ is considered. The spectral data consist of the eigenvalues of the Neumann--Dirichlet problem for the operator $-c^2(x)\partial_x^2$ together with their derivatives with respect to a Robin parameter at the boundary. We propose a two-step recovery procedure. In the first step, the Neumann-to-Dirichlet map $Λ$ is reconstructed from the spectral data using the results of arXiv/0406582. In the second step, the reconstructed $Λ$ is used within the regularization strategy for the boundary control method presented in arXiv:1509.04478. As an improvement, the regularization of the control problems employs a weighted combination of $L^2$ and $H^1$ penalty terms, and we prove a uniform convergence result for the family of optimal controls, thereby allowing the regularization parameters to be tuned simultaneously. We also prove that the forward spectral map, which assigns to a wave speed its spectral data, is Lipschitz continuous, and that the inverse spectral map underlying the reconstruction procedure is Hölder continuous on a subclass of wave speeds. The method is implemented numerically and validated on both smooth and piecewise smooth wave speed profiles. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the recovery of the wave speed exhibits high accuracy and robustness.
comment: 51 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Code available at https://github.com/pkulikov239/bcm-inverse-spectral
☆ Global Existence of Strong and Weak Solutions to the 2D Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System in Bounded Domains with Large Data and Vacuum
Yingzhi Du, Huijiang Zhao
We study the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system in a general simply connected bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions and a positive, possibly non-flat, doping profile. We establish the global existence of a unique strong solution and of a global weak solution for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum when the shear viscosity is a positive constant and the bulk one proportional to a power of the density with the power bigger than 4/3. The main difficulties arise from the interaction between the Poisson force and the general boundary geometry. To overcome them, we introduce a modified material derivative and derive quantitative $L^p$ estimates for the density by means of a Neumann duality argument together with a harmonic correction generated by the Navier-slip boundary condition. We further obtain a pointwise representation of the effective viscous flux by pulling back the Neumann Green function on the unit disk through a conformal mapping. The resulting commutator estimates, combined with elliptic estimates for the Poisson equation, yield a uniform-in-time upper bound for the density and allow us to close the higher-order a priori estimates. Finally, the global weak solution is constructed through a charge-preserving approximation and compactness argument.

☆ Global Existence and Partial Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes System in a Half-Space
Yubo Chen, Jianbo Yu
We establish endpoint partial regularity for suitable weak solutions to the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Navier--Stokes system with constant sensitivity and linear consumption in a half-space under no-slip and no-flux boundary conditions. The full space--time singular set, including its boundary part, has vanishing one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This follows from a Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg type criterion at the natural $r^{-1}$ dissipation scaling, valid at interior and boundary points without additional pressure smallness. The key estimate combines weighted mass control with the localized entropy--energy inequality to close the iteration without a separate $n\log n$ quantity and accounts for the mass term generated by rescaling. Boundary-compatible pressure and caloric decompositions yield local Hölder regularity. We also prove a lower-order criterion requiring smallness only of the velocity, signal gradient, and pressure oscillation, with a threshold depending on an arbitrary finite density mass bound. We construct global suitable weak solutions under natural entropy and energy assumptions without smallness restrictions on the initial data. The potential is time-independent with bounded gradient; boundedness of the potential itself is assumed only for the large-time results. If its gradient is also Hölder continuous, a solution can be selected to become bounded and classical throughout the closed half-space after a finite waiting time. For the same solution, we obtain decay and Neumann Gaussian asymptotics for both scalar components without initial spatial moment assumptions. The profile coefficients are the conserved bacterial mass and the limiting signal mass, respectively, and the latter is strictly positive whenever the initial signal is nonzero.
☆ Non-resonant angles in a Robin eigenvalue problem
Konstantin Pankrashkin
In an earlier study of the Laplacian eigenvalues with strongly attractive Robin boundary conditions in polygons it was found that if each corner is either concave or non-resonant, then the asymptotic behavior of the individual eigenvalues is determined by an effective one-dimensional operator on the boundary with Dirichlet boundary conditions at the corners. The non-resonance condition was formulated in terms of an eigenvalue bound on truncated sectors, and it was only shown to be satisfied by the right and obtuse opening angles. In the present work, we determine the full range of non-resonant angles: it turns out that the non-resonance condition fails only for the opening angles $\fracπ{2n+1}$ with $n=1,2,3,\dots$, and these critical values are equivalently characterized in terms of the jumps of the eigenvalue counting function and the existence of bounded generalized eigenfunctions. This resolves the numerically supported conjecture stated by Dauge and Lafranche.

☆ The conformal Poisson embedding method for the anisotropic Calderón problem with a potential
Cătălin I. Cârstea, Tony Liimatainen, Yi-Hsuan Lin, William Trad
We prove that the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $Δ_g+q$ determines a compact connected real-analytic Riemannian manifold of dimension at least three and a real-analytic real-valued potential, up to a diffeomorphism fixing the observed boundary and the conformal gauge of the equation. The result is new even when \(q\) is constant, i.e. for the fixed-frequency (Helmholtz) equation \(Δ_g u+λu=0\). The measurements are restricted to an arbitrary nonempty open boundary set $Γ$. ☆ Boundary stabilization of multi-dimensional first-order quasilinear hyperbolic systems
Haitian Yang
We study the long-time behaviour of multi-dimensional first-order symmetrizable quasilinear hyperbolic systems with nonlinear feedback boundary conditions. Assuming strict interior and boundary Lyapunov inequalities for the linearized system and non-characteristic boundaries, we prove global existence for small initial data and exponential H^s decay, with s>d/2+1 an integer. We consider both bounded smooth domains and flat periodic cylinders, and illustrate the results with physical examples and numerical simulations.
☆ Identifying secondary critical mass levels in two- and higher-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
Yulan Wang, Michael Winkler
The parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} u_t = Δu - \nabla \cdot (u\nabla v), \\[1mm] 0 = Δv - μ+ u, \qquad μ:=\frac{1}{|Ω|} \int_Ωu, \end{array} \right. \qquad \qquad (\star) \] is considered under homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions in the ball $Ω=B_R(0)\subset {\mathbb R}^n$, where $n\ge 2$ and $R>0$. The main results identify a mass level $m_\star(n,R)>0$ as critical in the sense that $\bullet$ whenever $0m_\star(n,R)$, then any solution of ($\star$) emanating from nonnegative and nonconstant continuous radial initial data $u_0$ with $\int_{B_R} u_0=m$ and $\frac{1}{|B_r|} \int_{B_r} u_0 \ge \frac{m}{|B_R|}$ for all $r\in (0,R)$ blows up in finite time. The value of $m_\star(n,R)$ can be determined in an essentially explicit manner in dependence on principal zeroes of appropriate Bessel functions of the first kind; in particular, $m_\star(2,R)\approx 14.68197 \cdot π$ for all $R>0$. Accordingly, as a supplement to known mass-dependent blow-up dichotomies these findings reveal a genuinely secondary critical mass phenomenon for ($\star$) especially also in its two-dimensional version in which no precedent of this form seems known.
☆ Hölder regularity of solutions to parabolic equations associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators

In this paper, we study Hölder regularity of local weak super-solutions to the parabolic equation associated with fractional $p$-Laplacian type operators $$ \partial_t u(t,x)-\text{p.v.}\int_{\R^d}|u(t,y)-u(t,x)|^{p-2}(u(t,y)-u(t,x))J(t;x,y)\,dy=0,\quad (t,x)\in \R\times \R^d, $$ where $\text{p.v.}$ denotes the principal value, $p\in(1,\infty)$ and the kernel $J(t;x,y)$ is comparable (uniformly with respect to $(t;x,y)\in\R\times\R^d\times\R^d$) to the fractional $p$-Laplacian kernel $|x-y|^{-d-sp}$ with $s\in(0,1)$. Our contribution extends the fundamental work of Kassmann and Weidner to the nonlinear case $p\ne 2$. In particular, we provide an explicit nonlocal parabolic tail condition in terms of an $L^{1+\varepsilon}$-norm in the time variable (for a suitable $\varepsilon>0$) for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, under which Hölder regularity holds. Our proof is based on the method of expansion of positivity, which is the key ingredient in the reduction-of-oscillation argument.

☆ Short scale asymptotics in nonlocal spectral problems
Volodymyr Rybalko, Antonina Rybalko
We study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of nonlocal convolution-type operators $$L_\varepsilonρ=-\frac{1}{\varepsilon^{d}}\int_ΩJ\left({\frac{|x-y|^2}{\varepsilon^2}}\right)ρ(y)dy+a(x)ρ(x),$$ (with a continuous sufficiently fast decaying at infinity function $J\geq 0$) when the scaling parameter $\varepsilon>0$ tends to zero. Assuming that the minimum of the function $a(x)$ is attained at a point $x_0\in \overlineΩ\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and is non-degenerate, we establish several terms in the asymptotic expansion of the first eigenvalues $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}$ of $L_\varepsilon$. If $x_0$ is an interior point of the domain $Ω$, we show that $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilonμ^{(k)}+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$, where $μ^{(k)}$ are eigenvalues of a harmonic oscillator (obtained by the blow up analysis), the corresponding eigenfunctions of $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon$ are concentrated near $x_0$ on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$. If $x_0\in\partial Ω$ then the asymptotic expansion of the eigenvalues of $L_\varepsilon$ has the form $λ_\varepsilon^{(k)}=a(x_0)-1+\varepsilon^{2/3}Λ_0+\varepsilon(μ^{(k)}+αp_0)+\overline{o}(\varepsilon)$. The corresponding eigenfunctions are represented as the product of a function depending on the distance to $\partialΩ$ and concentrated on the scale $\varepsilon^{2/3}$, and functions localized on the scale $\varepsilon^{1/2}$ and asymptotically independent of the distance to $\partialΩ$. The latter functions converge (after rescaling) to eigenfunctions of a harmonic oscillator (in tangential variables), $μ^{(k)}$ being their eigenvalues. The former function is given, to the leading term, by the scaled Airy function, and $Λ_0$, $α$ and $p_0$ depend on $J(|x|^2)$ and $a(x)$.
☆ Blocking of bistable front propagation: Application to Wolbachia population replacement
Saoussen Latrach, Nicolas Vauchelet, Hatem Zaag
In order to control epidemics of mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, for which there is still no vaccine available, several strategies aim to directly target the mosquito population. One technique involves introducing a symbiotic bacterium called Wolbachia into the population, which blocks the transmission of pathogens. A mathematical model of the introduction of this bacterium and the replacement of the mosquito population with a population carrying this bacterium has been developed, proving that in a homogeneous environment, there is spatial propagation of the replacement. The objective of this paper is to study the blocking of this propagation in cases where the environment is not homogeneous. In particular, we are considering scenarios where the environmental carrying capacity varies significantly across different regions of the spatial domain. To achieve this objective, we first reduce the original 2x2 reaction-diffusion system to a single closed equation, providing a simplified framework for studying the dynamics of Wolbachia propagation. We then investigate the blocking of the propagation in the population replacement process, focusing on the effects of spatial variations in the environmental carrying capacity. Numerical simulations have been performed to validate the theoretical results.
☆ Weighted Liouville Theorems and A Priori Bounds for Indefinite Superlinear Equations with Pucci's Maximal Operator
Karan Rathore, Mohan Mallick, Ram Baran Verma

We consider second-order strictly hyperbolic operators whose coefficients are Lipschitz continuous in space and may oscillate near the initial time. By combining Tarama's energy with frequency-dependent weights, we prove an energy estimate without loss for $α=0$ and with a stretched logarithmic upper bound for the loss when $0<α<1$, which implies an arbitrarily small loss in the Sobolev scale. These estimates extend the analysis of Colombini, Del Santo and Fanelli [\emph{Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa Cl. Sci. Zdzislaw Brzezniak, Benedetta Ferrario, Margherita Zanella
We consider the Navier-Stokes equations in a smooth bounded domain $D\subset \mathbb R^3$. It has been proved in arXiv:2609.08284 that these equations have a unique solution - globally defined in time - when a superlinear noise is introduced and the initial velocity belongs to the space $V$ of divergence-free $H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^3)$-vector fields. Here we show that the same result holds when there is also an additive noise and a deterministic forcing term. Moreover, when the deterministic forcing term is time-independent we prove the existence of at least one invariant measure for this stochastic equation. This is obtained by the Krylov-Bogoliubov method, based on tightness and Feller property in $V$. Finally, we show that the set of invariant measures contains one ergodic invariant measure.

We consider the Cauchy problem on the real line for a one-dimensional transverse-field isentropic non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system with viscosity $μ(ρ)=αρ^δ$, $0<δ\leq1$, and vacuum at spatial infinity. The viscosity therefore vanishes precisely where the density vanishes. We establish two global large-data theorems, one for the sublinear range $0<δ<1$ and one for the linear case $δ=1$, in a nontrivial invariant class of magnetic fields. The class is described by the frozen-in flux $h=b/ρ$ and its mass derivative $k=ρ^{-1}h_x$. The key identity $[\partial_t+u\partial_x,ρ^{-1}\partial_x]=0$ transports both $h$ and $k$, removes all negative powers of the density from the Lorentz force, and propagates the magnetic regularity. A modified effective-velocity entropy contains an additional coercive magnetic term, while its only error is controlled by $k$. Magnetic pressure also strengthens the density upper bound. These estimates close the large-data continuation argument in the ranges $0<δ<1$, $γ\geqδ+\tfrac12$, and $δ=1$, $γ>\tfrac32$. As a result, we extend the work of Cao, Li, and Zhu (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 2022) from the Navier-Stokes equations to the MHD equations.

Feimin Huang, Yi Wang, Jian Zhang
We investigate the time-asymptotic stability of composite waves consisting of a non-classical Liu shock and a rarefaction wave for non-convex viscoelastic system. By choosing delicate time-dependent shift functions to the viscous shock and suitable weight functions for the relative entropy, we succeed in proving the time-asymptotic stability of the composite of a viscous Liu shock and a rarefaction wave from two different characteristic families for the one-dimensional viscoelastic system with a cubic non-convex stress-strain relation by $a$-contraction method. Here the non-classical Liu shock can be either degenerate or non-degenerate, which can be seen as the system version of the scalar Oleinik shock. Note that both the shift and the weight functions are chosen quite differently in the two cases of nearly degenerate and fully non-degenerate. The paper represents the first time-asymptotic stability result for the composite waves consisting of both non-classical Liu shock and rarefaction wave from two different families for the non-convex physical system.

Applied to Xu's recent qualitative $C^{1,1/3}$ regularity for planar infinity-harmonic functions, we obtain uniform interior $C^{1,β}$ estimates for every $0<β<1/3$. Our construction employs time-dependent absorbing sets while ensuring exponential attraction among the constructed sets. Moreover, we show that the resulting exponential attractors are uniform-that is, they remain stable under perturbations. As an application of this abstract theory, we study the weakly damped hyperbolic equation with sub-quintic nonlinearity. Using the proposed approach, we construct exponential attractors for the process generated by the Shatah-Struwe solution, which satisfies both energy and Strichartz estimates. Furthermore, we establish the Holder continuity of these exponential attractors with respect to the external forcing term.
